title: Remove repeated causal, binding, and staging work from library execution
description:
## Objective and authorization

Deliver a bounded Mossignal execution optimization that removes whole-history
provenance copying and rehashing, repeated validation of published bindings, and
duplicate copies of a private staged successor. Preserve the standalone library's
causal, inspection, persistence, replay, temporal, and atomic-failure guarantees.

This is the native delivery record for the cross-repository brief
`mossmoot:moss-o3ff.1` in `/Users/mikkofinell/code/mossmoot/.beads/issues.jsonl`.
The motivation is `/Users/mikkofinell/code/mossmoot/docs/scratch/trap_foundation_review.md`,
especially its first two sections. The brief and motivation are task provenance,
not normative Mossignal authority. Baseline: clean `main`, accepted commit
`207cd9758682f49ad6457776560972512c669a56`; all prior native beads were closed.

The design is independently accepted below. Implementation requires a separately prepared, reviewed and assigned bounded bead; this epic is not an unlimited coding assignment. This is separately bounded future work, not a
restart of the retired continuation roadmap. No push is authorized here.

## Confirmed costs

At this baseline, `transaction.rs::build_ready_provenance` copies and remaps every
previous record before appending a reaction. `finalize_provenance_build` hashes
the whole graph to obtain its view scope and rewrites every reference again.
`state_digest.rs::ProjectionContext::build` indexes and hashes all records in the
machine and episode views before selecting the relevant closure, independently
for successive digest queries. `checkpoint_migration` makes every old record a
supporter of the topology-change record, even records unrelated to current facts.

`binding.rs` constructs a complete owned InputProjector on each facade call:
completeness is rechecked and caller identifiers are cloned despite the complete
immutable published binding invariant. `Machine::stage` makes one store clone,
then `apply_advance` clones many of the same fields into local working state.
These are source-confirmed work shapes, not measured latency or throughput claims.

## Concrete design proposal

### Shared immutable causal nodes

Use a private causal store of immutable shared nodes. Each frozen node holds its
inspection record, strong handles to its immediate predecessors, its canonical
payload, and its CauseDigest. Runtime state and transient builders hold private
owned cause handles; the public CauseRef remains Copy and opaque. Give references
a private lineage namespace and non-reused node key. A successor or forecast
shares immutable ancestors and creates new nodes without rebasing their keys.
Restoration builds a fresh private namespace from validated content identities.

A view owns a finite root set and therefore its backward closure, rather than a
prefix vector or a strong link to the preceding view. Public lookup validates
the namespace and membership in that view's closure. A lazily built immutable
membership index may serve inspection; ordinary execution must use its owned
cause handles and must not build that index by scanning history. Shared ancestors
may resolve in multiple owning views. A candidate-only or foreign-machine cause
must never resolve through the predecessor view. Keep precise structured lookup
failures; no durable public arena index, new public trait, or unsafe pointer API.

Freeze nodes after all semantic fields, pending keys, deadlines, stamps, and
predecessors are final. Compute canonical bytes and the content digest once from
cached predecessor digests. Normalize subjects to their stable qualified identity
under the creating topology, so later topology changes cannot reinterpret a
flat key. Do not intern logical records in the first slice; coalescing identical
canonical bytes during artifact projection remains supported, with multiplicity
and labeled relations intact. Any digest collision with different bytes remains
fatal corruption, never an arbitrary cache hit.

Lookup/collision registries, if needed, hold weak node references. Remove dead
entries when the corresponding node is released; a weak-key table accumulating
one entry per past reaction is still a leak. Release unreachable DAG nodes with
an iterative worklist in safe Rust, including long chains, rather than recursive
Arc destruction. No node points strongly to the arena registry or previous view
in a way that creates a retention cycle. Storage/allocator mechanics may be
refined by implementation provided this ownership and cost model is preserved.

### Retention roots and release

Maintain an explicit retention-root inventory, separate from the canonical
digest/artifact root manifest. Live roots include authoritative external levels;
stored state and establishment/latest-transition causes; current operation and
port facts exposed by inspection, including last-reaction evidence; output
baselines; pending scheduling origins; edge, transport, inertial, and periodic
facts; active diagnostic beginning/current evidence; and required module facts.
Existing standard-module last-reaction facts remain correctly labeled inspection
evidence, with all contained causes owned; they are not a new historical archive.

Each TransactionResult owns roots for every cause in its entire change set and
event stream, including intermediate-deadline reactions, diagnostics, and source
revision events in a patch transaction. Every owned inspection, explanation,
episode, and forecast artifact independently owns the roots for all causes it
exposes. An episode view must not incidentally retain an old complete machine
view. Keeping an old standalone result alive intentionally keeps its closure
alive. Dropping it releases only its ownership; shared live or other owned roots
still retain their complete ancestry.

Replacing a live root releases the old closure only where no other root owns it.
No full arena sweep is required at every advance. A stateless fixed circuit with
no externally retained results should release unrelated old reaction records.
Toggle establishment chains, periodic phase ancestry, pending causes, preserved
state, and independently retained artifacts may legitimately grow. No constant
memory guarantee is made for such required ancestry, and no ancestry is silently
truncated. The existing public controls are ownership/drop and the required-growth
budget; no general public prune/checkpoint method or historical-retention selector
is currently implemented. The specifications permit optional collection and
explicit authoritative checkpoints, but this delivery adds neither a checkpoint
API nor a history-disable mode. Automatic release of unreachable optional nodes
is a private storage choice justified for any library consumer.

### Digests, persistence, and migration

Separate execution projection from full closure enumeration. Execution facts
obtain cause-content identities directly from their owned handles; they need no
scan or rehash of all retained causal records. Observable projection and snapshots
walk only their required root closure, read cached canonical node bytes, sort by
CauseDigest, and preserve collision checks and complete self-contained ancestry.
Memoize the committed execution/observable digests when the immutable semantic
successor and its root manifest are finalized. Repeated pure queries reuse those
values. Keep the canonical reference encoder callable in tests and debug checks.

An observable digest or snapshot still emits the required closure: its work is
proportional to relevant semantic bytes, not constant time. Retained external
artifacts and unrelated arena records do not enlarge that projection. Do not
replace the specified canonical digest with a new Merkle-root digest merely to
make emission constant time.

At migration, preserve the existing authoritative source-fact encoding for
removed subjects, migration/reset rules, original pending ancestry, and explicit
checkpoint boundary reporting. Create source checkpoint wrappers for the selected
source closure using cached source canonical content. Make TopologyChange depend
on the current source roots required to explain that transition (excluding externally retained historical artifact roots), rather than every historical allocation.
Pass this new topology-change handle explicitly through transaction-local
construction; remove the reverse scan for a matching patch record.

The rooting change is deliberate and must be reviewed as a general library
choice: migration no longer turns otherwise unreachable optional records into
required supporters. Required explanations remain complete to initialization or
the already-declared migration/checkpoint boundary. This is not a policy to erase
causally required history. Cache/storage-only stages preserve accepted version-2
canonical inputs. If adopting the narrower TopologyChange projection changes its
canonical semantic interpretation, use a coherent new provenance/digest domain
version and relevant artifact version vector and goldens in that bounded slice,
as required by machine-state-digests::projection-version-rule. No compatibility shims,
old-version decoder, or release freeze is needed. The independent acceptance section below settles the exact version surface for the reclamation child.

Charge required-provenance growth from the transaction-local count of newly
required logical records at the existing accounting boundary. Do not use the net
change in live records: collecting old nodes cannot cancel current growth, and a
cache hit or physical sharing cannot change success/failure. Preserve all other
policy limits and identity cursors. Snapshot restoration validates all roots,
payloads, cycles, subjects, bounds, stamps, versions, and digest claims before
building the new shared store; private caches never replace those checks. Replay
continues through ordinary apply, and snapshot, replay, and forecast artifacts
retain their existing explicit roles.

### Published binding proof and one successor

Validate exact context, uniqueness, kinds, and completeness at BoundMachine
construction, rebind, and target-binding publication. Retain that proof with the
immutable map/context. Facade initialize/advance borrow this validated mapping
through a private projection helper instead of reconstructing the public owned
InputProjector. Keep public standalone projector behavior intact. Check every
supplied identifier, kind, duplicate/conflict, required snapshot level, exact
NetworkKey/fingerprint/schema, runtime revision, execution freshness, and patch
target context at the appropriate admission boundary. Do not add Hash/Ord bounds
to caller identifiers. Linear Eq lookup per submitted observation remains valid;
this proposal removes repeated completeness scans and success-path identifier
copies, not all identifier lookup costs.

Capture predecessor execution identity, revision, baseline/establishment facts,
and the evidence needed for change comparison before consuming staged fields.
Make one private semantic successor per outer transaction. Move or mutate its
owned fields rather than cloning the same collections into another workspace.
Evaluate each chronological reaction against its immediate predecessor and
consume owned evaluation outputs after their necessary borrows end. One full
initial live-state copy is acceptable; sparse overlays and persistent calendars
are outside this delivery. Retain the shared evaluator for apply, bound apply,
forecast, and replay. No public Machine clone/fork or mutable facade escape.

Prepare migration, result provenance, output/diagnostic projection, digests, and
all budget checks before the single non-fallible publication. Any evaluation or
projection failure drops the entire successor and preserves the predecessor's
machine and binding map, including ordered occurrences and public event cursors.
Private namespace allocation/cache activity is non-semantic; it must not expose
candidate records through an old view or consume public identities on failure.

## Contract basis and evidence

New drafts requiring independent review:
- `mossignal.provenance.retention` — `docs/specs/contracts/provenance-retention.yaml`:
  root closure, optional collection, and operational budget distinction.
- `mossignal.verification.optimized_paths` — `docs/specs/contracts/optimized-path-verification.yaml`:
  executable references, normalization, rollback observations, and debug evidence.

Existing reviewed represented facets reused without edits:
- `mossignal.provenance.causal_explanations` — `docs/specs/contracts/causal-explanations.yaml`:
  current support versus transition and authoritative retention boundaries.
- `mossignal.inspection.semantic_projection` — `docs/specs/contracts/semantic-inspection.yaml`:
  owned cause lifetimes, current facts versus explicit reaction evidence, query purity.
- `mossignal.binding.live_reconfiguration` — `docs/specs/contracts/live-bindings.yaml`:
  immutable complete bindings and projection before publication.
- `mossignal.binding.application_adapter` — `docs/specs/contracts/application-bindings.yaml`:
  checked caller identifier projection and owned results.
- `mossignal.identity.machine_state_digests` — `docs/specs/contracts/machine-state-digests.yaml`:
  canonical projection, private-identity exclusion, collision handling, version inputs.
- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_artifact` — `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-artifact.yaml`:
  self-contained causal closure, framing, required observation, versioned vectors.
- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_restoration` — `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-restoration.yaml`:
  strict validation, fresh private handles, round trip and future sufficiency.
- `mossignal.persistence.replay_artifacts` — `docs/specs/contracts/replay-artifacts.yaml`:
  ordinary replay fold, exact operational identity, optional-history exclusion.
- `mossignal.runtime.transaction_forecast` — `docs/specs/contracts/transaction-forecast.yaml`:
  shared evaluator and unchanged borrowed predecessor.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy` — `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`:
  explicit limits and atomic accounting boundaries.
- `mossignal.reconfiguration.atomic_replacement` — `docs/specs/contracts/atomic-topology-replacement.yaml`:
  migration, source causes, loss policy, and publication.
- `mossignal.runtime.ordered_reactions` — `docs/specs/contracts/ordered-reactions.yaml`:
  stamped origins, once-only deadline maturity, episode identities, rollback.
- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`:
  chronological deadline batches, pending identity, and schedules.

Task-scoped evidence status found changed cited sections only in machine-state-
digests, machine-snapshot-artifact, machine-snapshot-restoration, and runtime-policy.
Rechecked their affected rules against the current execution projection,
uninitialized snapshot, pending-event records, and runtime diagnostic catalogue.
The added last-reaction/origin stamps are governed by the unchanged reviewed
ordered-reactions contract; the missing/invalid policy-limit mappings remain
unchanged in meaning. Reuse those combined facets without silently refreshing
reviewed hashes or rewriting historical initial-version guidance. The selected
contracts' adjacent known-uncovered checkpoint/optional-history/public-cursor
facets are outside this delivery unless expressly described above.

## Proposed implementation slices after design review

1. Shared immutable causal nodes and cached canonical content, retaining existing
   logical root selection initially. Replace scope remapping and whole-history
   hashing; preserve current canonical bytes and reference lookup isolation.
2. Root ownership and automatic optional-node release, including views, episode
   ownership, iterative destruction, weak-index cleanup, and migration source
   roots. Adopt the independently settled version surface if required.
3. Borrowed facade input projection and one private successor workspace. This
   depends on the shared-handle representation but does not require a new public
   projector or sparse evaluator. Keep eval/projection failures atomic.
4. Complete projection integration and cross-feature refinement/cost evidence:
   root-selected snapshot/digest indexing, committed digest memoization, strict
   restoration, forecast/replay, migration, and finite repository acceptance.

These are proposed bounds, not created or approved implementation beads. The
reviewer may reorder integration to keep every intermediate accepted revision
coherent; no partially migrated cause representation may be published. Code
agents remain sequential. Each later bead must name its concrete reference,
affected invariants, and bounded acceptance matrix rather than inherit the epic
as unlimited scope.

## Deterministic verification and cost evidence

Retain an independent test-only full-record/canonical encoder and clone-and-swap
executor. Compare normalized semantic observations, output/change/diagnostic
streams, original stamps, pending identities, schedules, explanation boundaries,
and canonical bytes/digests where the projection interpretation is unchanged.
When the reviewed migration projection changes, use the newly specified
root-directed canonical reference and test that omitted records are optional;
do not simply regenerate goldens to hide a difference.

Use test-only work counters, not timing thresholds: records copied/remapped,
old/new record payload hashes, complete-binding validations, identifier clones,
full successor copies, closure records/bytes emitted, live node/index counts,
and reclaimed nodes. Assert zero old-record rewrite/hash work on ordinary
advance, no whole-map clone/completeness pass on successful facade calls, and
one outer successor copy rather than a second full working-state copy. Distinguish
new logical records and required closure emission from avoidable history work.

Exercise fixed stateless circuits over increasing reaction counts with no old
views retained (live records/index entries should remain bounded by live facts
and current reaction evidence), the same runs retaining old results (each old
view must still explain its own causes), then selective and complete drops.
Include a legitimately growing Toggle/phase ancestry chain and long iterative
release, branching forecasts, converged foreign-machine histories, same-time
pulses and due batches, cancellation, changed current support with unchanged
output, module facts, diagnostic begin/update/resolve, topology removal/reset/
preservation, pending migration, snapshot/restore continuation, and replay.

Fault-inject provenance/result/digest preparation and the existing private bound
projection seam; compare complete predecessor observation on every failure.
Check all affected budgets below/at/above their boundary, especially new-record
growth when many old nodes are reclaimed. Add focused failing cost/regression
tests first and observe the baseline failure before fixing each defect. Run the
narrow relevant tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`; accepted code uses
`make check-final`, closed bead state and synchronized `.beads` in one semantic
commit. Long fuzz campaigns remain separate unless a later bead requires one.

## Surface and exclusions

Expected implementation surface: `transaction.rs`, `machine.rs`, `state_digest.rs`,
`binding.rs`, `inspection.rs`, `episode.rs`, standard-module facts, `persistence.rs`,
`snapshot_restore.rs`, `replay.rs`, private causal helpers, affected tests and
canonical vectors, and only independently justified version/document changes.
Start with private modules; no additional crate or dependency is required.

No Mossmoot edits, trap mode, history-disable policy, host reaction purge,
parallel evaluator, user callback, persistence migration shim, generic borrowed
projection framework, automatic authoritative checkpoint, new public history
archive, or benchmark-driven throughput claim. Host trap-history purge is a
separate coordinator/Mossmoot responsibility. Discarding a host result cannot
erase ancestors still required by a live library state or pending event.

## Readiness and review decisions

No conflicting requirements, missing fundamental semantics, or frozen
compatibility promise blocks a deterministic design. The independent review
must assess root completeness and view isolation, weak-registry cleanup and
iterative release, stable subject/canonical caching through migration, the
TopologyChange root/version choice, budget accounting, and executable cost and
refinement evidence. These are concrete design acceptance decisions within
implementation freedom, not requests to disable existing library guarantees.
Keep this delivery blocked on its design-review bead; create no implementation
children and make no implementation commit during preparation.


## Independent coordinator acceptance — 2026-10-09

The two new contracts were independently checked against every cited heading and relevant adjacent causal-explanation, owned-inspection, migration and digest-version rules. Corrected optimized-path verification so documenting/supplementing unavoidable reference-independence limitations remains mandatory rather than merely recommended. Both contracts are reviewed with current source fingerprints. Existing unchanged reviewed facets remain reused; no unrelated source hashes were refreshed.

Approved representation and ownership:
The immutable-node/private-handle/shared-ancestor model, source-qualified canonical caching, root-owned isolated views, weak-index cleanup and safe iterative release are accepted implementation choices. Enumerate every exposed CauseRef root, including all intermediate-deadline and pre-patch result events and diagnostic beginning/current evidence. An old result or forecast owns only its own closure; no view-prefix or previous-view chain. Query-side membership caches cannot add semantic roots or mutate execution. Dead weak registry entries must be reclaimed; failure must not expose candidate nodes through predecessor views or consume semantic public IDs.

Exact migration root decision:
At the post-earlier-deadline/pre-patch source boundary, TopologyChange supporters are the deduplicated current SOURCE machine retention-root manifest described above (external origins, stored-state establishment/latest-transition and edge/temporal facts, current operation/port and explicitly represented last-reaction facts, baselines, pending scheduling roots, active diagnostic evidence and current module facts), preserving every required source closure and source-qualified fact wrapper. The union is current source truth, including facts explaining removed/reset subjects, not all arena allocations. Independently retained results, inspections or forecasts are NOT inputs to this manifest. Merely holding or dropping such an artifact cannot alter a later patch, machine digest, budget outcome or snapshot projection. This delivery adds no policy-selected optional history or retention mode. Remove the ambiguous parenthetical allowing externally selected historical supporters. Required ancestry is not truncated; a migration/source checkpoint continues to expose its declared boundary. Add an equivalence test where otherwise identical machines retain different unrelated old result handles and still produce identical semantic patch results/digests.

Canonical version decision:
Storage/sharing/cache-only changes preserve the accepted version-2 canonical interpretation and bytes. Adopt the narrowed TopologyChange supporter interpretation in the root-reclamation slice with provenance_semantics_version 3, provenance-record digest-domain version 3, execution/observable digest-domain versions 3 and machine projection_version 3. This is a domain-version change, not a new digest suite. Keep the existing digest suite, canonical encoding, artifact/envelope schemas, core/node/diagnostic and physical patch-state semantics versions unchanged where their definitions are unchanged. Snapshot/replay semantic-version vectors and strict restoration checks must consistently admit the mixed current component vector (provenance 3, unchanged components 2), and reject unsupported vectors; split the current blanket version constant as necessary rather than gratuitously incrementing unrelated semantics. Update affected versioned vectors against the independent new root-directed canonical reference, not blind golden regeneration. No old-version decoder, upgrader, compatibility shim or inferred release freeze is required. If implementation reveals an actual separately changed schema/semantic component, return that concrete delta for review rather than silently expanding the version change.

Coherent implementation ordering:
Slice 1 migrates shared immutable causal representation, stable view references and cached canonical node content across ALL consumers that must understand those values, including current explanation, episodes, result ownership, digest encoding, snapshots, restoration, forecast and replay. Retain existing logical root selection initially, but this intermediate accepted revision must be fully correct and preserve version-2 canonical bytes. Required representation adapters belong in this slice, not an eventual integration cleanup.
Slice 2 implements current-root ownership/reclamation, independent artifact lifetimes, bounded weak metadata and iterative release, together with the approved migration supporter/version change and all corresponding persistence/replay validation.
Slice 3 implements borrowed published binding projection and one isolated successor with unchanged supplied-input/freshness checks and complete core/bound-projection rollback. It may use the established shared handles; no sparse evaluator/calendar framework is included.
Slice 4 is only remaining projection/memoization optimization and cross-feature cost/refinement acceptance. It must not defer correctness or mandatory format support from slices 1–3. Create only the next bounded implementation bead initially, using concrete executable references, supported input domain, failure matrix and focused cost counters; later tasks may be refined from implementation evidence.

Acceptance qualifications:
Required ancestry and deliberately held old artifacts may legitimately grow. Full canonical observable/snapshot emission remains proportional to relevant semantic closure bytes. New required-provenance growth is charged independently of reclaimed old records, sharing or cache hits. Current inspection/last-reaction evidence remains the library's contract, not an execution archive imposed by an application. No trap-specific policy, history-disable API or Mossmoot change is authorized. Ordinary Eq/Clone identifier API bounds stay unchanged. Evaluation, result/digest construction and bound output/diagnostic projection all finish before publication.

Design is accepted; no implementation has run or been accepted. Native review ms-hks can close, ms-0ap stays open. A subsequent bounded preparation pass may author the first implementation bead; coordinator reviews that concrete brief before coding.
acceptance_criteria: Independent design review accepts the ownership/root and canonical-version choices and both draft contracts; only then author bounded implementation children. Delivered code must preserve required library semantics and demonstrate deterministic cost reduction with independent refinement evidence and complete finite acceptance checks.

title: Share immutable causal records across views and version-2 consumers
description:
## Objective, baseline, and route

Implement ONLY accepted `ms-0ap` slice 1: shared immutable causal representation,
stable private cause references and owned views, and cached canonical node
content. Migrate every necessary consumer in one coherent accepted revision.
Remove ordinary advance's rewriting of prior records and recomputation of their
canonical content while preserving the current version-2 semantics and bytes.

Parent: `ms-0ap`, independently accepted by closed design-review bead `ms-hks`.
Read its complete "Independent coordinator acceptance — 2026-10-09" section;
it supersedes the earlier provisional slice wording. This task is native to
Mossignal, with cross-repository provenance `mossmoot:moss-o3ff.1`; no foreign
repository work is included. Authoring baseline: clean `main` at
`64845860d89a4fad542067372ce20a21b5916926`. This is separately bounded work,
not a retired-roadmap item. The coordinator has independently reviewed this brief and authorized this bounded slice; claim it before implementation.

## Included representation and coherence obligations

1. Introduce private immutable causal nodes with owned predecessor handles,
   stable qualified semantic subjects, a frozen inspection record, canonical
   version-2 payload and CauseDigest. Freeze after stamps, pending identities,
   deadlines and every predecessor/contribution field are final. Compute a new
   node's payload/hash once from cached predecessor content identities; prior
   immutable node content is shared, not copied, rebased or rehashed on advance.
   Keep supporter roles, unordered normalization, ordered relations and counted
   contributions exactly as the current version-2 encoder defines them. Do not
   intern logical records in this slice; canonical artifact coalescing remains
   unchanged and cannot erase contributor multiplicity or logical growth units.

2. Public CauseRef remains opaque and Copy, with coherent equality/hash/order
   traits. Use the accepted private lineage namespace/non-reused key model;
   preserve ancestor identity within shared lineage without exposing a durable
   arena position. A view independently owns its selected graph closure and
   validates namespace plus membership. Cloning a view shares immutable storage.
   Reject foreign and unpublished branch-only references through the appropriate
   structured lookup path. Query-side membership caches cannot add machine
   roots, admit candidate records, or alter semantic observation. Do not compute
   view identity by hashing or remapping the entire historical graph.

3. Preserve the current MACHINE logical retained-record set and canonical root
   selection for this intermediate revision, including the version-2 migration
   rule in which TopologyChange supporters cover the source logical record set.
   Keep that set explicit and machine-local; it is not all allocations in a
   shared arena or the union of external artifact views. Storage may retain a
   private logical record catalogue until slice 2; it must share immutable nodes
   without a strong chain of prior views. Creating or holding unrelated result,
   inspection or forecast artifacts, and allocating hypothetical/failed nodes,
   must not change later live patch results, digest inputs, budgets or snapshots.
   Do not narrow TopologyChange supporters, collect optional machine history,
   add selected-history policy, change checkpoint boundaries, or adopt version 3.

4. Enumerate and adapt every internal/public cause-bearing consumer. Live facts
   include external origins, operation/port support and last-reaction evidence,
   state establishment/latest transition, baselines, edge/temporal/phase and
   cancellation facts, pending scheduling origins, active episode evidence, and
   standard-module public/internal/reset/toggle/capture facts. Each returned
   transaction owns every cause in its complete change set and event/diagnostic
   stream, including all earlier deadlines and source events preceding a patch.
   Owned inspections, explanations, module facts, diagnostic episodes and
   forecasts retain their own sufficient views. Future machine updates, owner
   removal, or machine drop cannot invalidate a still-owned artifact. Do not
   replace this with a view-prefix or predecessor-view retention chain.

5. Replace ordinal/scope/vector assumptions in current explanation and cause
   lookup, state digests, snapshot production, strict restoration, results,
   episodes, standard-module facts, forecasts, replay and bound-result ownership.
   Required representation adapters and format support all belong here; no
   correctness work may be left for slice 4. Persistence still uses CauseDigest
   and self-contained canonical closure, never private namespace/key values.
   Restoration validates hostile graph input, canonical content, cycles, roots,
   subjects, versions, stamps, budgets and claimed digests before publishing a
   machine with fresh private references. Cached data is not validation evidence.

6. At the existing migration boundary, retain source-qualified version-2 fact
   wrappers and the existing supporter selection. Construct new immutable
   migration/checkpoint records and translate the relevant private references
   without mutating old source nodes or interpreting their flat keys against the
   target topology. Preserve original pending ancestry, explicit reset/migration
   facts, source-output events, explanation boundaries and canonical ordering.
   A new wrapper is distinct from the old record retained by an old artifact.

7. Keep every current policy accounting boundary and success/failure result
   unchanged. In particular, physical node allocations, cache hits, namespace
   issuance, membership/index construction and sharing are not provenance-growth
   units. Version-2 migration replaces existing logical records with source-fact
   wrappers before appending other records; preserve that logical accounting,
   rather than charging each replacement wrapper as a new physical allocation.
   Ordinary append growth, public pending-event cursor, same-time reaction order,
   and all below/exact/over budget results must remain equivalent to the baseline.

8. Keep the existing transaction evaluator and staging/publication strategy.
   All fallible provenance, result, digest and core/bound projection preparation
   finishes before publication. Evaluation, restoration or projection rejection
   cannot expose candidate graph membership, alter old owned views, or consume
   semantic public identities. Forecast stays read-only; replay stays ordinary
   apply. Shared private cache activity may be non-semantic, but must not become
   an input to the machine's roots, canonical state or admission decisions.

9. Provide safe teardown for the new ownership graph and failed/hypothetical
   allocations as part of representation correctness. Deep owned ancestry must
   drop without recursive stack overflow or ownership cycles. Any weak lookup/
   collision registry cleans dead entries and cannot leak one entry per failed
   forecast or dropped artifact. Automatic pruning of the live machine catalogue
   and its bounded-current-root memory proof are reserved for slice 2; currently
   selected live ancestry may still grow. Do not promise bounded total history.

## Canonical equivalence boundary

Preserve accepted version-2 provenance semantics, provenance/execution/observable
and snapshot digest domains/projections, component vectors, artifact/envelope
schemas, canonical encoding and digest suite. No blanket version bump, golden
regeneration, old-version support, compatibility shim or freeze is in scope.
All existing golden inputs/artifact bytes remain unchanged. Add version-2
fixtures for covered cases absent from the current vectors rather than replacing
existing expectations. Digest comparisons alone are insufficient: compare the
complete canonical inputs and artifact bytes with the independent reference.

The approved mixed-component version-3 root-reclamation decision in `ms-0ap`
belongs to a later bead. This slice creates no new canonical interpretation and
does not silently narrow required closure or change a schema to ease adaptation.

## Executable references and normalization

- Maintain a test-only uncached version-2 canonical graph encoder based on the
  accepted `state_digest.rs` record/relationship encoding. It walks semantic
  records and predecessor relations using stable subjects and recomputes payloads
  and hashes independently of production cached bytes, cached hashes and view
  membership indexes. Retain the straightforward vector/full-graph form as its
  reference data model; sharing the primitive CBOR writer and semantic enums is
  acceptable, sharing the optimized cache or lookup algorithm is not. Compare
  every frozen node's content and both full machine digest inputs, including
  migration source-fact wrappers, to this executable reference.
- Keep the existing clone-and-swap/full topological execution path as the
  transaction reference; this bead does not optimize those algorithms. Compare
  apply/forecast on private predecessors and replay through a sequential ordinary
  fold. Shared evaluator semantics are intentional; this reference alone cannot
  prove the new representation. Supplement it with the independent uncached
  canonical encoder, explicit expected ancestry fixtures, direct membership/
  retained-owner tests, and complete before/after rejection observations. Record
  any other independence limitation and its mandatory supplementary evidence.
- Fresh inspection/root enumeration is the observation reference. Normalize by
  stable/qualified subjects, semantic record kind/payload, labeled predecessor
  content, multiplicities, stamps, current support versus latest transition,
  retention boundary, public pending keys and diagnostics. Exclude private
  namespace/key/ordinal/layout differences. Do not normalize away a missing
  required ancestor, changed contribution, event order, budget failure, or
  canonical byte difference. New private IDs must not replace the normative
  output or artifact comparison.
- Use maintained snapshot encode/decode/restore and ordinary replay tests plus
  fixed version-2 bytes as artifact references. Round trips must also continue a
  compatible future transaction sequence and compare complete required semantics.

All references must be callable in ordinary tests and generated differential
cases. Keep independent debug recomputation of cache content, closure ownership,
acyclicity and digest equality available at meaningful commit/restore boundaries.

## Exact acceptance matrix

Use focused fixtures plus bounded generated valid graphs/histories over existing
primitive/standard-module families, level and counted-pulse input, non-regressing
times with repeated same-time reactions, equal deadlines, existing policies and
prepared patches. Exercise the following matrix, with canonical/reference
comparison where applicable:

| Area | Successful cases | Failure and retained-artifact cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lifecycle/current facts | Declared uninitialized snapshot; initialization; empty and unchanged ready inputs; changed support with unchanged output baseline | Wrong lifecycle, network/schema, revision and expected execution digest preserve complete predecessor; old initialization/current inspection still resolves |
| Pulse/state | Counted merge/joint support and unordered permutations; Toggle, set/reset and SampleHold establishment/preservation | Count overflow, rejected conflict and required-growth boundary; prior stored/latest-transition and pulse event artifacts preserve full counted ancestry |
| Temporal/order | PulseDelay, TransportDelay, InertialDelay and Periodic; several earlier deadlines, exact-deadline due/fresh batch, repeated time, cancellation and preserved phase | Late budget/time/order rejection rolls back all prior internal work; retained scheduling/due/result causes remain stamped and resolvable |
| Modules/diagnostics | Nested qualified module facts; reset/toggle/capture views; episode begin/material update/resolve | Old module and episode views survive later mutation/removal and machine drop; every exposed current or beginning evidence cause resolves |
| Topology | Initialization and ready patches; due-before-patch source events; preserve/reset/remove state and pending work; source checkpoint wrappers | Stale/invalid patch or migration loss rejection; old source results remain inspectable; version-2 patch bytes and accounting stay unchanged |
| Ownership/branches | Clone views; retain several results/inspections/forecasts through later commits; restore fresh private owners | Foreign/converged-machine refs and branch-only refs cannot resolve through an old view; unsuccessful candidates leave no visible membership; deep final-owner drop and dead weak metadata cleanup |
| Artifact independence | Identical live machines with different unrelated old result/inspection/forecast handles held or dropped execute the same patch and future sequence | Canonical patch results, state digests, budget outcomes and snapshot bytes are identical regardless of those external handles; discarded hypothetical allocations stay absent |
| Snapshots/replay | Existing uninitialized/family goldens; ready pending/episode/module/migrated snapshots; round trip plus future history; successful forecast/apply and replay | Existing malformed/missing/cyclic/colliding provenance, invalid subjects/versions/stamps and digest claims reject with no partial machine; forecast/replay failures preserve their ordinary guarantees |
| Core/bound publication | Core and bound results own all cause-bearing output/diagnostic fields and correct source/target labels | Inject provenance/result/digest preparation and the existing private bound projection failures; machine/map, views, semantic identities and complete observation remain unchanged |

Capture complete rejection observation: lifecycle, topology/fingerprint, revision,
time/last stamp, external and settled levels, stored/temporal state, pending keys/
origins/deadlines and next cursor, baselines, required causes/retention, module
facts, active episodes, execution and observable digests and canonical snapshot
where available. Compare before/after for all touched structured rejection
categories and all affected limits below/at/above the representable boundary.

## Deterministic cost evidence

Add test-only counters in the actual production path for copying/rebasing old
record payloads/references, whole-graph scope hashing, old-node canonical payload
encoding/hash recomputation, newly frozen-node encoding/hash, and closure records/
bytes visited/emitted. Run fixed circuits at increasing history lengths after a
committed prefix, including a legitimately growing stateful chain, and isolate
one ordinary advance (no patch, no restoration, no deliberately enabled debug
oracle). Require zero old-record rewrite/rebase work, zero whole-history view-scope
hashing, and zero recomputation of old-node canonical payload/digest. Each new
immutable node is encoded/hashed once; aliases/cache reads do not count as nodes.

Show the regression counters fail on the accepted old representation before the
fix, then pass with independent canonical equality. Verify retained ancestors
are physically shared across views and later commits; do not use a test-only
production bypass to satisfy the counters. Distinguish new migration wrappers
from recomputing old source content. Full observable/snapshot emission and any
remaining logical catalogue/index traversal may still scale with relevant
retained structure; report those remaining costs rather than claiming this
slice makes the complete transaction or digest constant time. Cold restore and
independent debug checks intentionally recompute/validate graph content.

## Contract basis

All named represented facets are reviewed and reused unchanged; this preparation
creates no contract draft or specification amendment.

- `mossignal.inspection.semantic_projection` — `docs/specs/contracts/semantic-inspection.yaml`:
  complete owned observation, retained-cause ownership, current versus history, purity.
- `mossignal.provenance.causal_explanations` — `docs/specs/contracts/causal-explanations.yaml`:
  current support versus transition, full authoritative ancestry, retention boundaries.
- `mossignal.identity.machine_state_digests` — `docs/specs/contracts/machine-state-digests.yaml`:
  content-addressed canonical graph, storage-independent subjects/order, collision and version rules.
- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_artifact` — `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-artifact.yaml`:
  framing, current facts, self-contained closure and unchanged canonical vectors.
- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_restoration` — `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-restoration.yaml`:
  hostile validation, fresh private references, round trip and future sufficiency.
- `mossignal.persistence.replay_artifacts` — `docs/specs/contracts/replay-artifacts.yaml`:
  ordinary fold, exact identity, artifacts and optional-history exclusion.
- `mossignal.runtime.transaction_forecast` — `docs/specs/contracts/transaction-forecast.yaml`:
  shared transition, owned candidate and predecessor-preserving success/failure.
- `mossignal.runtime.ordered_reactions` — `docs/specs/contracts/ordered-reactions.yaml`:
  occurrence stamps, temporal origin/phase, episodes and identity rollback.
- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`:
  grouped chronological deadlines, pending identity and schedule facts.
- `mossignal.reconfiguration.atomic_replacement` — `docs/specs/contracts/atomic-topology-replacement.yaml`:
  source facts, migration/reset, loss policy and atomic publication.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy` — `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`:
  unchanged logical accounting and boundary/rollback tests.
- `mossignal.binding.live_reconfiguration` — `docs/specs/contracts/live-bindings.yaml`, and
  `mossignal.binding.application_adapter` — `docs/specs/contracts/application-bindings.yaml`:
  contextual constraints on cause-bearing projected results and prepublication failure.
- `mossignal.provenance.retention` — `docs/specs/contracts/provenance-retention.yaml`:
  contextual distinction between required roots, optional storage and operational limits;
  collection and retention configuration remain outside this slice.
- `mossignal.verification.optimized_paths` — `docs/specs/contracts/optimized-path-verification.yaml`:
  executable independent references, normalized evidence and complete rollback matrix;
  unavoidable independence limitations require supplementary verification.

Both new accepted contracts have unchanged cited evidence. Existing historical
changed-source flags in digest/snapshot/restoration/policy contracts are exactly
the already-reconciled facets accepted in `ms-0ap`: current ordered-reaction
stamps supplement those represented rules, and policy missing/invalid-limit
meanings remain unchanged. No governing source changed since the accepted design.
Do not reopen unchanged reviewed facets or refresh hashes. Their adjacent
known-uncovered public checkpoint/history-selector/new-cursor facets are not
required by this representation-only task.

## Surface, freedom, exclusions and completion

Expected surface: private causal helpers; `transaction.rs`, `machine.rs`,
`state_digest.rs`, `inspection.rs`, `episode.rs`, standard-module cause/history
adapters, `persistence.rs`, `snapshot_restore.rs`, `replay.rs`, affected bound
result adapters if necessary, and existing/focused conformance, ownership,
canonical and differential tests. Preserve public method responsibilities and
ordinary caller identifier bounds. Use private modules and the simplest safe
deterministic representation. Internal container/namespace/index mechanics and
test-helper names remain implementation freedom; no new crate is required.

Excluded: automatic machine root pruning, narrower migration supporters,
version-3 fields/domains/vectors, optional-history selection/checkpoint APIs,
borrowed facade projector optimization, duplicate successor-copy removal,
whole-machine digest memoization, sparse evaluators/calendars, new public fork or
callbacks, Mossmoot code/docs/beads, additional agents, throughput promises,
compatibility layers and push. Fix only representation adaptation needed for
coherence; ordinary private choices do not require a specification amendment.

There is no fundamental semantic or compatibility blocker. The unavoidable
decomposition boundary is producer/consumer coherence: CauseRef/view/digest
adapters cannot be independently left broken in an accepted intermediate revision.
Legacy machine logical retention remains intentionally unchanged until slice 2;
that permits the accepted version-2 patch and growth behavior to remain exact.

After coordinator brief review and code authorization, follow sequential
implementation rules: failing meaningful cost/regression checks first, focused
tests while iterating, `make check-dev`, then `make check-final` for acceptance.
Do not weaken an oracle or gate. Record the concrete private choices and residual
costs, then leave the bead in_progress and implementation uncommitted for the
coordinator's independent corrective acceptance review. Closure, flush and the
normal accepted semantic commit follow that review. Do not
close the parent epic or independently promote discovered draft contract changes.
Authoring this brief itself makes no implementation, commit or push.


Coordinator brief acceptance (2026-10-09):
Read the full concrete scope and acceptance matrix against the accepted ms-0ap design. Approved as one representation-coherent slice: all required consumers migrate together, exact version-2 canonical semantics remain, logical live-machine retention is separate from external artifact ownership, and growth accounting preserves logical rather than allocation units. The references and cost counters distinguish representation savings from remaining full-closure work. No new contract facet or fundamental blocker was found. Implementation is now authorized only for this bead. Retention pruning/version 3 and projector/staging changes remain later. Independently review all implementation and any discovered draft contracts before acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: After coordinator brief review and separate code authorization: all cause-bearing consumers use one coherent immutable shared representation; current machine logical record/root selection, policy accounting and version-2 canonical inputs/artifact bytes are preserved; retained and foreign/branch-owned views satisfy the explicit matrix; executable uncached canonical and ordinary transaction references pass; real-path counters demonstrate zero prior-record remap/scope hashing and zero old canonical content recomputation on ordinary advance; required focused checks and make check-final pass before one accepted implementation commit. No root-reclamation/version-3, binding/successor optimization or whole-machine digest-memoization scope is included.
notes:

Review-ready uncommitted proposal on main at accepted baseline 6acb565f226bf4f07802e14aa4f01052bb7e80f0. Implementation scope is ms-0ap.1 only. Leave in_progress for the coordinator's independent corrective acceptance; closure, final flush, staging and accepted semantic commit remain with that review. No push.

Private immutable nodes own predecessor handles and once-frozen version-2 canonical payload/digest. Explicit machine-local logical catalogues preserve legacy retention and growth accounting. Reaction allocation batches retain exact ancestor CauseRefs while isolating hypothetical/new branch records. Verification includes maintained uncached vector/linear-lookup canonical reference, full canonical execution/observable inputs and snapshot envelopes, unchanged/new version-2 fixtures, counted and mixed temporal/stateful generated histories, rollback at provenance/result/projection seams, owner/foreign-branch isolation, retained history through quiet patches/removal/drop, forecast reclamation, and a 30,001-node drop on a 64 KiB stack. title: Implement reaction-scoped pulse foundation with Merge
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 24 as one bounded vertical slice: introduce reaction-scoped Pulse transport through the established public authoring, validation, dependency, compilation, evaluation, input-artifact, machine, and transaction layers, using Merge as the first pulse primitive.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contracts governing this slice

- `mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/reaction-scoped-pulse-foundation.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs pulse batch semantics, typed endpoints, pulse observations in exact-bound inputs, reaction storage and fan-out, initialization and ready transactions, Pulsed events, checked overflow, grouped provenance, verification, and the pre-stability fingerprint extension boundary.
- `mossignal.node.pulse_merge`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/pulse-merge.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs the first variadic pulse primitive, its checked summation law, stable port multiplicity, authoring, causality, compilation, evaluation, diagnostics, provenance, and conformance.

### Reviewed contracts reused unchanged where their recorded evidence remains unchanged

- `mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition`, `mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder`, `mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports`, and `mossignal.diagnostics.collections`
  - role: established canonical authored graph, typed builder ownership, artifact suppression, and deterministic diagnostic collection boundaries.
- `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_dependency_graph`, `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_cycle_validation`, `mossignal.compile.compiled_network`, and `mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator`
  - role: established dependency, acyclicity, compilation, and full-reference settlement patterns extended by pulse incidences.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle`, `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction`, `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction`, and `mossignal.runtime.policy`
  - role: established lifecycle, atomic publication, exact transaction binding, provenance ownership, and budget patterns retained while adding reaction-scoped pulse facts.
- `mossignal.runtime.level_input_snapshot`, `mossignal.runtime.level_input_delta`, `mossignal.identity.input_schema_fingerprint`, and `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint`
  - role: established exact-bound input artifact and semantic identity boundaries extended to typed pulse endpoints under the explicit pre-stability projection policy.

The two pulse contracts have completed independent review at their recorded evidence baselines. No changed reviewed-contract rule is being silently reused as pulse authority.

## Included scope

- Extend typed and dynamic authored definitions with external Pulse inputs and outputs, stable pulse ports and connections, and the closed Merge node kind.
- Add convenience and exact keyed builder forms for pulse endpoints and Merge, preserving builder ownership, stable variadic port identity, and immediate duplicate-key rejection where determinable.
- Extend structural validation, duplicate-source and empty/unary advisories, reaction dependencies, cycle validation, compilation descriptors, invariant checks, and full topological settlement for Pulse and Merge.
- Extend exact-bound InputSnapshot and InputDelta builders with typed pulse observations; absent pulse inputs mean zero and never require establishment.
- Add reaction-scoped pulse counts to initialization and ready-machine execution without retaining them as current machine state after a reaction.
- Publish deterministic Pulsed output events with exact count, time, revision, and result-resolvable grouped provenance, including initialization pulses.
- Reject checked Merge overflow atomically as `runtime.pulse_count_overflow`.
- Extend the pre-stability network and input-schema fingerprint projections to represent Pulse signal kinds, pulse endpoints and ports, and Merge; synchronize the authoritative exact projections, applicable contracts, and affected golden vectors in the accepted change.
- Add permanent focused pulse-foundation and Merge conformance verification.

## Explicit exclusions and non-goals

- No Coalesce, Zip, PulseGate, PulseSelect, PulseRoute, edge detector, Toggle, latch, sample-hold, stateful, or temporal primitive.
- No previous or proposed state, persistent pulse value, pending event calendar, schedule, temporal deadline, or topology patch.
- No module, standard catalogue, binding projector, persistence artifact decoder, replay, snapshot restoration, or reconfiguration implementation.
- No incremental dirty propagation, optimized sparse evaluator, retained pulse history, subscription delivery, or complete explanation rendering.
- Do not change PulseCount representation or add wrapping, saturating, or infallible arithmetic.
- Do not add callbacks, trait-object evaluator extension, implicit Pulse and Level conversion, or a splitter primitive.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement `reaction-scoped-simultaneous-count`, `checked-fixed-width-count`, `typed-pulse-boundaries`, `exact-bound-pulse-inputs`, `fanout-and-reaction-settlement`, `lifecycle-transaction-integration`, `external-pulse-publication`, `overflow-is-atomic-rejection`, `grouped-pulse-provenance`, `pre-stability-pulse-identity-extension`, and `pulse-foundation-verification` from the pulse-foundation contract.
- Implement every requirement of `mossignal.node.pulse_merge`.
- Reuse the existing authoritative graph, validation report, dependency graph, compiler, machine lifecycle, transaction, runtime-policy, and provenance paths; do not create parallel pulse-only lifecycle or execution architectures.
- Preserve the exact existing level behavior and level-only transaction observations while widening the same input artifacts and reaction executor to pulse batches.
- Keep each stable pulse incidence distinct through authoring, validation, canonical identity, compilation, evaluation, and grouped provenance.
- Treat pulse count zero as semantic absence for the reaction while retaining duplicate-observation and schema-validation guarantees during input construction.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose the simplest deterministic private pulse slot, batch, descriptor, evaluator, and grouped-provenance representations.
- Choose and test one deterministic locally allocated Merge port order and record it at close-out; exact keyed forms remain available for durable independent reconstruction.
- Either retain explicit zero pulse observations or normalize them after validation, provided semantic results and duplicate-observation behavior are unchanged.
- Choose the simplest exact pre-stability canonical extension consistent with the existing record and tagged-variant style, then synchronize its specification text, applicable contract representation, and golden vectors in the accepted change. No historical reader or migration is required before stabilization.
- Extend existing failure evidence minimally when `runtime.pulse_count_overflow` remains structured and identifies the failed pulse arithmetic sufficiently.

## Expected change surface

- Signal-aware authored and builder endpoint/node families.
- Structural validation, reaction dependency extraction, cycle integration, compilation, full evaluation, machine storage, transactions, provenance, and output events.
- InputSnapshot and InputDelta pulse construction and schema membership.
- Pre-stability network and input-schema fingerprint projections and golden vectors.
- Focused unit, integration, and conformance tests.
- The two reviewed pulse contracts only when implementation discovers reusable specification-backed corrections or records the accepted exact projection; such changes still require independent review before acceptance.
- Synchronized bead state at implementation acceptance.

## Required verification

1. Build pulse input to Merge to pulse output networks through both typed and dynamic public authoring paths and compare validation, compilation, fingerprints, initialization, and later transactions.
2. Cover Merge empty, unary, multi-input, permutation, duplicate-source, and fan-out cases with counts zero, one, two, and a larger representable value.
3. Verify initialization and ready pulse batches, omission as zero, explicit zero behavior, input insertion-order invariance, same-time event ordering, exact Pulsed counts, and no pulse persistence into later reactions.
4. Verify pulse and level endpoints remain kind-safe; unknown, duplicate, wrong-kind, wrong-network, foreign-schema, and stale-schema input failures preserve existing structured categories.
5. Verify Merge dependencies participate in cycle rejection and deterministic topological compilation with stable subject correspondence.
6. Verify grouped provenance retains each contributing port and count without invented order and every event CauseRef resolves through its result.
7. Test checked arithmetic at maximum representable boundaries; overflow rejects the complete transaction with `runtime.pulse_count_overflow` and a complete before/after machine comparison.
8. Verify same-topology insertion-order fingerprint invariance, sensitivity to Pulse versus Level schema and structure, exact Merge representation, and updated hand-reviewed golden bytes and digests.
9. Run narrow focused tests while iterating, then `make check-dev` and `make check-final`.

## Blocking questions

None. The exact pre-stability projection spelling and private pulse representation are bounded deterministic implementation choices, not frozen compatibility or missing semantics.

## Readiness

Ready for implementation against the two reviewed pulse contracts and reused reviewed foundations. This bounded bead has completed contract review; no product or design blocker prevents implementation progress.
notes: Implemented the bounded Pulse foundation and Merge vertical slice across typed/dynamic authoring, validation and cycle dependencies, deterministic compilation/evaluation, exact-bound pulse snapshots/deltas, initialization and ready transactions, Pulsed events, grouped port/count provenance, and atomic checked overflow. Locally allocated Merge input ports follow immediate IntoIterator order; exact-keyed ports remain reconstruction authority. Explicit zero observations are retained through input construction for duplicate/conflict validation and evaluate semantically as reaction-local zero without machine persistence. Extended the pre-stability version-1 canonical projection with merge, pulse, and reaction_scoped tags, synchronized authoritative spec text, reviewed affected contract records, and hand-reviewed golden bytes/digests. Added typed/dynamic equivalence, cycle, arity, multiplicity, fanout, lifecycle, schema-failure, provenance, ordering, fingerprint, and overflow tests. Corrective acceptance review rejected cross-kind external-output/source definitions during structural validation and strengthened maximum-count, complete failure-atomicity, permutation, advisory, mixed-event-order, and input-order coverage. make check-dev and make check-final pass. Affected contract edits completed independent evidence review.
close_reason: Implemented reaction-scoped Pulse transport and variadic Merge with synchronized specifications, focused conformance coverage, and passing final gate

title: Expand the standard catalogue with AtMost and AllEqual
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Continuation Roadmap item 38 by extending the accepted standard catalogue with canonical stateless `AtMost` and `AllEqual` descriptors, construction paths, inspection, diagnostics, identity, and exhaustive conformance while preserving `Exactly` and the ordinary module execution boundary.

## Roadmap provenance

- Document: `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`
- Item: 38
- Title: Stateless standard-module expansion

This provenance records task sequencing only. Authoritative specifications and the referenced contracts govern semantics.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed feature contract accepted for reuse

- `mossignal.standard.stateless_expansion`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/standard-stateless-expansion.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs AtMost and AllEqual identity, interfaces, total laws, dependencies, exact expansions, typed construction, diagnostics, inspection, explanation, and exhaustive conformance.

### Reviewed contracts accepted for reuse without modification

- `mossignal.standard.catalogue_foundation` (`docs/specs/contracts/standard-catalogue-foundation.yaml`): catalogue identity and discovery, declarations, canonical keys and fingerprints, dynamic construction, ordinary instantiation, diagnostics, inspection, and verification hooks.
- `mossignal.standard.exactly` (`docs/specs/contracts/standard-exactly.yaml`): accepted first-descriptor pattern and regression boundary; Exactly semantics remain unchanged.
- `mossignal.node.level_combinational_expansion` (`docs/specs/contracts/level-combinational-expansion.yaml`) and `mossignal.node.variadic_all` (`docs/specs/contracts/variadic-all.yaml`): Constant, Not, Any, All, and AtLeast semantics, typed ports, stable variadic multiplicity, validation, compilation, and settlement used by the canonical expansions. Only unchanged primitive-law and execution facets are reused; changed historical fingerprint evidence is not needed here.
- `mossignal.module.instantiation_hierarchy` (`docs/specs/contracts/module-instantiation-hierarchy.yaml`) and `mossignal.module.aware_execution` (`docs/specs/contracts/module-aware-execution.yaml`): generic typed instantiation, hierarchy, lowering, runtime behavior, provenance, and observation.
- `mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint` (`docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml`) and `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint` (`docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`): semantic definition and containing-network identity; standard declaration projection remains governed by the catalogue foundation.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model`, `mossignal.diagnostics.subject_references`, `mossignal.diagnostics.collections`, and `mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports`: structured evidence, stable subjects, deterministic coexistence and merging, and blocking artifact omission. Existing standard diagnostic categories are reused without contract changes.

## Included scope

- Add exact AtMost and AllEqual descriptors to canonical catalogue discovery order with their provisional semantic and expansion version 1 identities, fixed result roles, variadic Level interfaces, and threshold schema only for AtMost.
- Generalize catalogue-backed dynamic validation and generation across the three implemented descriptors without weakening malformed-request retention, deterministic finding collection, or LibraryDefect handling.
- Generate the exact canonical AtMost and AllEqual primitive case tables with deterministic stable keys, roles, expansion fingerprints, dependency signatures, and standard-origin module fingerprints.
- Add concise and explicit-keyed AtMost and AllEqual constructors to NetworkBuilder and ModuleBuilder, retaining equivalence with dynamic catalogue construction and generic ModuleDef instantiation.
- Add module-level diagnostics with exact empty, unary, constant-result, and duplicate-source coexistence and suppression behavior; prevent redundant primitive and unused-input warnings created solely by canonical implementation structure.
- Extend structured module inspection and explanation with AtMost allowance or excess facts and AllEqual common-value or mixed-group facts while preserving exact declaration, hierarchy, internal roles, and primitive drill-down.
- Execute both modules solely through existing generic module compilation, primitive evaluation, transactions, budgets, provenance, and inspection.
- Add deterministic descriptor and expansion checks plus exhaustive bounded-domain conformance for both modules, including preservation of existing Exactly behavior.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No stateful or temporal standard module, including resettable toggles or sample-hold.
- No new primitive node kind, privileged evaluator, callback, hidden simplification, module-specific transaction, hidden state, or pending work.
- No primitive aliases, builder-only conveniences, metadata-only conveniences, or application binding layer.
- No persistence envelope or decoder, restoration, snapshot/replay integration, topology patch, module replacement, descriptor-version migration, state migration, or internal-edit enforcement.
- No complete generic prose renderer, generated documentation system, editor palette, query planner, or subscription system.

## Implementation obligations

- Reuse the reviewed `mossignal.standard.stateless_expansion` contract as the module-specific semantic and conformance baseline.
- Reuse and generalize the existing catalogue, declaration, canonical key derivation, fingerprint, validation, builder, inspection, and ordinary module-runtime paths rather than creating descriptor-specific parallel infrastructure.
- Preserve the exact specified canonical expansions even when a smaller or behaviorally equivalent primitive graph exists.
- Keep catalogue and descriptor versions provisional under the repository pre-release policy; synchronize the current inventory and identities without compatibility shims or migration ceremony.
- Canonicalize variadic public keys by stable identity, preserve duplicate-source multiplicity, and ensure deterministic unique internal keys and roles independent of request insertion order.
- Keep malformed dynamic requests caller-representable and collect every independent safe finding deterministically; produce a ModuleDef only when blocking diagnostics are absent.
- Preserve existing Exactly declarations, fingerprints, diagnostics, construction, execution, and inspection except for deliberate catalogue-wide representation generalization that remains semantically identical and tested.
- Record non-obvious canonical case and derivation invariants with brief SPEC traces; production code remains free of unwrap and expect.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose the smallest deterministic descriptor dispatch and shared helper structure; a compact enum or private table is acceptable when exact public descriptor identity and behavior remain unchanged.
- Share cardinality counting, variadic canonicalization, diagnostics, inspection, and expansion helpers where module-specific laws and permanent roles remain explicit.
- Choose compact private structured inspection and explanation value shapes that expose every required fact; complete prose rendering is outside this task.
- Choose the simplest deterministic larger-arity property strategy supported by current test tooling, and record the concrete choice in tests or close-out.

## Expected change surface
