title: Execute user modules through ordinary runtime machinery
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Continuation Roadmap item 36 as one bounded capability slice: recursively lower validated user-module instances into the existing primitive compiled/runtime machinery while preserving instance-qualified identity, hierarchy, fingerprints, causality, atomicity, and supported runtime observation.

## Roadmap provenance

- Document: `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`
- Item: 36
- Title: Module-aware compilation, execution, and observation

This provenance records task sequencing only. Authoritative specifications and the referenced contracts govern semantics.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contracts

- `mossignal.module.aware_execution`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/module-aware-execution.yaml`
  - role: governs recursive ordinary-primitive lowering, stable qualified correspondence, deterministic module compilation, retained compiled/runtime hierarchy, ordinary state and temporal ownership, atomicity, budgets, provenance, observation, and module-execution verification.
- `mossignal.module.instantiation_hierarchy`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/module-instantiation-hierarchy.yaml`
  - role: governs instantiation, binding, retained validated hierarchy, causality, and module-aware semantic identity. Its temporary compilation-boundary rule and now-covered lowering gap were independently retired in this planning pass.

### Additional reviewed contracts reused without modification

- `mossignal.compile.compiled_network` (`docs/specs/contracts/compiled-network.yaml`): validated-only compilation, immutable topology, stable identity, private dense layout, reaction correspondence, invariants, and deterministic compilation.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint` (`docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`): validated fingerprint ownership and canonical exclusion of private layout for its represented families; module-instance sensitivity is governed by `mossignal.module.instantiation_hierarchy`.
- `mossignal.runtime.stateful_reaction_foundation` (`docs/specs/contracts/stateful-reaction-foundation.yaml`): independent family state, previous/proposed state, current output, and atomic successor commitment.
- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution` (`docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`): exact-time pending work, due-event execution, cancellation, and schedule.
- `mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation` (`docs/specs/contracts/reaction-scoped-pulse-foundation.yaml`): simultaneous Pulse multiplicity and reaction-scoped clearing.
- `mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator` (`docs/specs/contracts/restricted-full-topological-evaluator.yaml`): ordinary primitive full-evaluation semantics and causal correspondence.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy` (`docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`): explicit work limits and complete budget-failure atomicity.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle` (`docs/specs/contracts/machine-lifecycle.yaml`): immutable compiled ownership, independent spawned state, initialization, and ready-machine boundaries.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports` (`docs/specs/contracts/artifact-reports.yaml`): compilation artifact/report behavior and blocking omission.

All governing contracts are reviewed at unchanged authoritative evidence baselines for the facets used here.

## Included scope

- Make both compile forms succeed for every otherwise supported validated user-module instance, including mixed containing primitives, multiple instances, and nested instances.
- Recursively lower module-local nodes, connections, public input bindings, and public output mappings into the existing primitive descriptors and dependency graph.
- Preserve complete instance-path plus module-local-key correspondence for internal nodes, ports, connections, state, temporal work, diagnostics, provenance, and supported inspection.
- Retain module instances, parent-child hierarchy, public interfaces, bindings, and canonical expanded subjects in compiled graph/inspection access even when execution is flattened.
- Execute lowered Constant, Not, All, Any, Parity, AtLeast, Select, Merge, Toggle, and PulseDelay through their ordinary existing reaction, state, pulse, temporal, transaction, provenance, and runtime-policy paths.
- Preserve exact Level and Pulse interface behavior, fan-out, simultaneous multiplicity, cross-boundary current-reaction causality, state barriers, and temporal barriers through arbitrary supported nesting.
- Keep each stateful and temporal primitive independent per instance path, including when several instances share one `ModuleDef`.
- Carry the validated `NetworkFingerprint` and `InputSchemaFingerprint` unchanged through compilation.
- Add owned user-module `ModuleInspection` with a public boundary view and grouped expanded internal view, and extend focused structural/runtime observation to identify supported module-qualified subjects and hierarchy.
- Remove the temporary `compilation.unsupported_module_instances` rejection, evidence/discriminator implementation, catalogue/API/specification text, and rejection tests; confirm no contract reintroduces the retired staged rule.
- Establish behavioral differential conformance between an explicit primitive graph and its module-wrapped equivalent after normalizing intentionally distinct identity and hierarchy.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No standard catalogue discovery, standard typed constructor family, generated standard modules, or new standard-origin behavior.
- No persistence envelopes, snapshots, restoration, replay, or module-qualified artifact encoding.
- No module replacement, topology patches, compatible revision migration, state migration, or pending-event migration.
- No module-specialized evaluator, callback evaluator, hidden module state, module-specific transactions, incremental module compiler, descriptor sharing optimization, or new crate.
- No complete generic inspection query planner, subscriptions, or complete explanation rendering beyond the user-module and currently supported primitive observation paths.
- No identity equivalence promise between an explicit primitive graph and a module-wrapped graph; only required behavioral equivalence.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement every represented requirement in reviewed `mossignal.module.aware_execution` while preserving reviewed `mossignal.module.instantiation_hierarchy`.
- Reuse one recursive lowering path for top-level and nested instances and the existing closed primitive descriptor/evaluator dispatch; module boundaries must not introduce runtime semantic variants.
- Resolve each module input from its exact binding and each module output from its exact internal mapping. Preserve kind, incidence, fan-out, Pulse counts, and conservative dependency edges.
- Use collision-free module-qualified logical identity. Dense indices and any derived private lookup keys remain revision-local implementation details and must not leak into public identity, diagnostics, provenance, or fingerprints.
- Allocate state slots, temporal ownership, event records, and causal subjects independently for every qualified primitive occurrence.
- Preserve one immutable compiled topology with independent spawned machines and a single failure-atomic transaction publication point.
- Count expanded primitive work through existing runtime budgets consistently with the equivalent explicit graph; rejection must publish no partial hierarchy-associated state or output.
- Retain the authored module hierarchy alongside any flattened executable projection for compiled graph access and supported runtime inspection.
- Remove the entire temporary unsupported-module surface unless implementation discovers a separately authoritative unsupported case; do not keep compatibility shims.
- Keep production code free of `unwrap` and `expect`, preserve structured failures, and add brief `SPEC:` traces only for non-obvious normative invariants.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose direct recursive flattening or an equivalent recursive descriptor builder, favoring the smallest deterministic extension of the existing compiler.
- Choose collision-free private derived keys, path interning, lookup maps, hierarchy indices, and descriptor ordering; record and test the chosen deterministic correspondence without exposing dense layout.
- Choose whether module bindings are resolved eagerly into a temporary canonical graph or directly into descriptors, provided error/report behavior, compiled invariants, and retained hierarchy are identical.
- Add the smallest typed module-qualified subject/reference values and owned `ModuleInspection` structures needed by existing graph, inspection, and provenance APIs. Broader query, subscription, and explanation frameworks remain future work.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/compile.rs` for recursive lowering, qualified descriptor correspondence, retained hierarchy metadata, endpoint resolution, and compiled invariants.
- `crates/mossignal/src/validation.rs` only to replace the temporary compile rejection boundary and expose/reuse already-validated dependency and definition data without revalidating semantics.
- `crates/mossignal/src/module.rs`, `crates/mossignal/src/key.rs`, and `crates/mossignal/src/authored.rs` for focused reusable qualified subject/path projections where existing values are insufficient.
- `crates/mossignal/src/machine.rs` and `crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs` for module-qualified state, pending-work, provenance, and supported runtime inspection ownership.
- `crates/mossignal/src/diagnostics.rs` and `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs` for temporary diagnostic retirement and deliberate public exports.
- `crates/mossignal/tests/module_instantiation.rs` to remove the staged rejection oracle and retain authoring/validation coverage.
- New focused integration tests for module compilation/execution/observation, plus existing compiler, machine, and transaction tests where their private oracles need qualified subjects.
- `docs/specs/api_and_semantics_spec.md`, `docs/specs/concrete_rust_api_surface.md`, and `docs/specs/exhaustive_diagnostic_code_catalogue.md` to retire only the explicitly temporary staged-boundary text and catalogue entry.
- The roadmap item state and synchronized `.beads` metadata.

Treat this as an expected surface, not permission for unrelated refactoring. If a required correction materially exceeds it, stop for renewed planning.

## Required verification

1. Verify module-free compilation metadata and runtime behavior remain unchanged.
2. Compile and execute single, multiple, mixed containing/internal, and at least two-level nested user modules over Level-only, Pulse-only, and mixed interfaces.
3. Compare explicit primitive and module-wrapped graphs for initialization, ready reactions, outputs, Pulse multiplicity, state successors, pending events, schedule, diagnostics, normalized provenance, budgets, and rejection outcomes while allowing distinct identity/hierarchy.
4. Verify exact binding/output resolution, cross-boundary fan-out, nested output projection, and no accidental connection to private internals.
5. Verify current-reaction causal chains across module boundaries, including reconvergence, stateful current outputs, true state barriers, temporal barriers, and nested paths.
6. Instantiate one stateful or temporal module more than once and prove independent state, pending events, deadlines, causes, and inspection subjects per instance path.
7. Exercise Toggle and PulseDelay inside nested modules through initialization, repeated transactions, direct time jumps, equal deadlines, cancellation/scheduling behavior, and exact overflow or budget failures.
8. Verify hierarchy and module-qualified nodes/connections remain discoverable after compilation and supported node, pending-work, output, and provenance inspection identifies the exact owning path.
9. Verify compilation and observations are invariant under network/module insertion order and deterministic hierarchy traversal; validate compiled static invariants for nested expansions.
10. Verify the compiled artifact retains the validated fingerprints exactly; private flattening/layout changes do not alter them, while instance/binding/module/hierarchy semantic changes retain existing sensitivity tests.
11. Capture complete machine observations before every applicable structured failure and prove failure atomicity for module-expanded overflow, time arithmetic, and runtime-budget boundaries.
12. Remove the item-35 compile-rejection tests and prove `compilation.unsupported_module_instances` no longer exists in production code, catalogue/API text, contract rules, or public diagnostic evidence.
13. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`; final acceptance additionally runs `make check-final`.

## Readiness

Ready and free of unresolved product semantics. Independent review promoted both governing contracts and confirmed this bounded bead against them. Ordinary private lowering/layout choices are implementation freedom, not blockers.

  - status: reviewed
  - role: starting checkpoint bytes and `SnapshotDigest`. Reuse the emitted version vector and canonical profile. Do not reopen it. Its replay exclusion is this bead.
- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_restoration`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-restoration.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: `CompiledNetwork::restore` is the only way to obtain a machine from snapshot bytes. Future-transaction sufficiency stays that contract's rule. Do not change restore. `DecodePolicy.replay_frames` is already a caller limit and is enforced by replay decode, not by snapshot decode.
- `mossignal.identity.machine_state_digests`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-state-digests.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: reuse `execution-projection`, `observable-extension`, and `equality-is-not-validation`. Replay compares those digests. It does not define them.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: exact replay uses the machine's existing `RuntimePolicyId` and budget failures. Do not bypass policy or invent a second limit set.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-lifecycle.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: replay starts from an existing machine lifecycle. It does not spawn a second lifecycle model.
- `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: initialization frames call the ordinary initialization transition. The contract excludes replay; do not reopen it.
- `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: advance frames call the ordinary ready transition, including failure atomicity.
- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: direct-jump and stepwise replay both use this calendar. Do not add a second scheduler.
- `mossignal.module.aware_execution`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/module-aware-execution.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: qualified module identity and events come from the ordinary flattened machine. Do not add a module evaluator.
- `mossignal.standard.catalogue_foundation`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/standard-catalogue-foundation.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: replay of an installed standard module keeps `one-canonical-expanded-module`. Do not replace a standard module in this bead.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: the log's starting fingerprint must equal the machine's network fingerprint.
- `mossignal.identity.time_domain`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/time-domain-identity.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: artifact, context, and machine name one `TimeDomainId`. Do not put a persistence trait on `D`.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.persistent_episodes`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/persistent-diagnostic-episodes.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: episode identity and transitions are part of replay equivalence. That contract excludes replay encoding; do not reopen it.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: new replay failures are catalogue `Problem` values. Do not add a string fallback.

Reviewed contracts that merely list replay as excluded stay unchanged. That exclusion is why this contract exists. Do not reopen them only to delete the note.

## Included scope

- Record a successful `initialize` or `advance` through the ordinary `Machine::apply` transition and retain an owned frame with the expected previous execution digest, expected revision, runtime policy id, transaction, resulting execution digest, resulting observable digest, and zero-based `frame_index`.
- Replay an ordered frame sequence on `&mut Machine` by calling `apply`. Stop at the first failed or divergent frame. Report frame index, time when available, expected and actual identities, and the underlying failure. A failed apply leaves the machine unchanged for that frame. A successful apply whose digest disagrees leaves the published machine in place.
- Accept a live machine or a machine produced by `CompiledNetwork::restore` when its time domain, network fingerprint, execution digest, observable digest, revision, and runtime policy id match the log before frame zero.
- Persist `replay_frame` and `replay_log` as standalone canonical artifacts, each embedding its children as complete standalone bytes. A frame embeds one `transaction_record`. That record embeds one `input_snapshot` or `input_delta` for the current patch-free transaction. Integrity uses `mossignal/artifact_integrity/v1`, not `SnapshotDigest`.
- Emit the same version vector as the current `machine_snapshot` encoder. Reject every other component as `persistence.unsupported_version` with no upgrader. Do not call that single-vector table a freeze.
- Enforce the existing `DecodePolicy`, including `replay_frames`. Hostile and noncanonical bytes use the existing persistence codes. Do not repair, sort a semantic frame sequence, or accept a human-readable projection as evidence.
- Distinguish the represented `replay.*` conditions in the reviewed contract. `replay.expected_revision_mismatch` applies at every frame whose expected revision differs from the machine, including the first. `replay.frame_reordered` is sequence, digest, or prior-state linkage, not a revision mismatch. Keep an underlying runtime failure's own code and add frame context. Register only codes this slice emits, and update the diagnostic catalogue and public failure inventory goldens.
- Concatenate two logs only when the contract's boundary identities match; otherwise `replay.logs_not_concatenable`. Preserve order and renumber `frame_index` in the resulting log.
- Replay equivalence does not require equal optional history or equal `SnapshotDigest`.
- Prove direct-jump replay matches stepwise deadline replay, including a concatenation boundary immediately before and after a deadline. Prove a user-module network and a standard-module network reproduce the ordinary transition's events and both digests.
- Keep golden canonical bytes for representative frames and logs, including digests. Prove frame order changes bytes and that non-semantic input insertion order does not.

## Exclusions

- Distributed consensus, live replication, arbitrary event sourcing, nondeterministic host callbacks, and performance-oriented log compaction.
- Topology-patch preparation or commitment, patch-bearing execution, standard-module replacement, and forecast-marked frames. Item 56 and later stay unstarted.
- Checkpoint bundles, chunk storage, streaming decode, schema upgraders, historical corpora, and a second evaluator.
- Standalone `transaction_result`, `migration_report`, definition, runtime-policy, and network-patch artifacts.
- Changes to snapshot payload spelling, restoration acceptance, or digest projection rules.
- Scheduled coverage-guided fuzz. Structured corruption tests are in scope; a long fuzz campaign is not.

## Implementation obligations

Follow the reviewed contract and the freedoms named there. In particular:

- One frame type carries the observable digest. Do not keep a second type that drops it.
- `apply_recorded`, or the same shape, clones only as needed and then calls `Machine::apply`. Do not copy the transition.
- In-place apply. No per-frame rollback. No ordinary `Machine::Clone`. No whole-sequence atomic helper unless a test forces it, in which case it still publishes only through the ordinary transition.
- Snake_case keys for conceptual fields, with the snake_case spellings already written by the persistence text kept as written. Record the chosen keys. They are not a freeze.
- `frame_index` is the position in that log, from zero, and is the non-semantic display index. Concatenation may renumber it and does not keep a second audit index. A gap is `replay.frame_missing`. A repeat is `replay.frame_duplicated`. A machine revision that differs from the frame's expected revision is `replay.expected_revision_mismatch` at every frame. An expected previous execution digest that disagrees with the machine after the log boundary, or a log starting execution digest or starting revision that disagrees with the first frame, is `replay.frame_reordered`. The log-to-machine boundary uses `replay.starting_execution_digest_mismatch`, `replay.starting_observable_digest_mismatch`, `replay.time_domain_mismatch`, `replay.network_fingerprint_mismatch`, and `replay.runtime_policy_mismatch`. Emit one replay code for a checkpoint, not the restoration persistence code of the same general name as well.
- Compute `ReplayLogContentDigest` under `mossignal/replay_log_content/v1` over the starting identities, each embedded frame's artifact integrity digest, any final identities, and the semantic version vector. Do not invent a frame-content domain or another domain label.
- Encoder omits a recorded transaction result and any patch attachment. A decoded `transaction_result` child fails before apply as `persistence.unsupported_version` of that child's artifact schema version, with kind `transaction_result` and no upgrader. A patch attachment fails as `replay.patch_preparation_diverged` before apply and without mutation. Do not implement result comparison or `prepare_patch`.
- Replay diagnostics may use the existing operation subject plus `ReplayEvidence`. Do not add `ReplayLog`, `ReplayFrame`, or `ReplayChunk` subject variants.
- Reuse `PersistenceContext`, `ArtifactBytes`, `DecodePolicy`, the CBOR profile, and the diagnostic registry. Recognized wrong kind is `persistence.malformed_envelope`. An unrecognized kind string is `persistence.unknown_artifact_kind`.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/persistence.rs` and, if clearer, one new private or public replay module. Re-export the deliberate public types from `lib.rs`.
- `crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs` for the recording helper and any `Clone` needed on `Transaction` and `InputSnapshot`.
- `crates/mossignal/src/diagnostics.rs` for the emitted replay codes, `ReplayEvidence`, and `ReplayFailure`.
- `crates/mossignal/src/snapshot_restore.rs` only if the shared decode helper must enforce `replay_frames` for replay artifacts. Do not change snapshot acceptance.
- Integration coverage in `crates/mossignal/tests/`, plus golden updates under `crates/mossignal/tests/golden/` for the catalogue, failure inventory, and replay artifact bytes.
- Do not edit reviewed contracts, including the replay contract, unless implementation finds a concrete contradiction. That edit returns the contract to `draft` for independent review and does not refresh reviewed hashes.

## Verification

Use the narrowest replay tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`. The accepting run is `make check-final`.

Required cases are the reviewed `history-and-verification` rule, which exercises `temporal-and-module-equivalence`, plus hostile decode, unsupported version, concatenation rejection, and runtime-failure atomicity. Do not weaken an existing golden or gate.

## Readiness

Ready. No blocker. Patch-bearing execution is `known_uncovered` because the ordinary patch path is a later roadmap item, not missing replay semantics for the current transaction model. Rejecting a patch attachment without executing it is the simplest deterministic choice and is not a compatibility freeze.
close_reason: Add deterministic replay over ordinary transactions, with frame and log artifacts, checkpoint checks, and concatenation.

title: Add level aliases and builder-only conveniences
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Continuation Roadmap item 39 as the supported level-only convenience slice: add xor, level_gate, majority, nand, nor, and xnor to both typed builders while preserving exact primitive lowering, ordinary identity, diagnostics, inspection, and execution.

## Roadmap provenance

- Document: docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md
- Item: 39
- Title: Supported aliases and builder-only conveniences

This provenance records sequencing only. The referenced contracts and authoritative specifications govern product semantics.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed feature contract

- mossignal.authoring.level_conveniences
  - docs/specs/contracts/level-conveniences.yaml
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs exact classification, lowering, semantic-boundary consequences, typed builder behavior, and conformance for the six level conveniences.

### Reviewed contracts reused without modification

- mossignal.node.level_combinational_expansion (docs/specs/contracts/level-combinational-expansion.yaml): Any, Parity, and AtLeast total laws, stable variadic multiplicity, typed authoring, diagnostics, causality, execution, and conformance. Only unchanged semantic, authoring, diagnostic, and verification facets are reused; changed historical fingerprint evidence is outside this task.
- mossignal.node.variadic_all (docs/specs/contracts/variadic-all.yaml): All total law, stable variadic multiplicity, authoring, diagnostics, causality, execution, and conformance. Only unchanged non-fingerprint facets are reused.
- mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator (docs/specs/contracts/restricted-full-topological-evaluator.yaml): ordinary Not law and complete primitive-graph settlement.
- mossignal.authoring.typed_module_builder (docs/specs/contracts/typed-module-builder.yaml): ModuleBuilder primitive-family parity, builder-scoped signals, foreign-signal rejection, canonical lowering, and ordinary validation.
- mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder (docs/specs/contracts/typed-network-builder.yaml): NetworkBuilder scope and structured foreign-signal failure behavior.
- mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint (docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml) and mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint (docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml): existing semantic graph identity and metadata exclusions. Only unchanged represented rules apply; changed unrelated validated-owner source evidence is not needed.

## Included scope

- Add concise NetworkBuilder and ModuleBuilder xor(a, b), level_gate(value, enable), and majority(inputs) primitive aliases.
- Lower aliases exactly to binary Parity, binary All, and AtLeast(floor(arity / 2) + 1) respectively, including majority([]) as AtLeast(1, []) and therefore Low.
- Add concise NetworkBuilder and ModuleBuilder nand(inputs), nor(inputs), and xnor(a, b) builder-only operations.
- Lower builder-only operations exactly to Not(All(inputs)), Not(Any(inputs)), and Not(Parity([a, b])) using only ordinary primitive authoring.
- Preserve immediate iterator consumption, stable per-port multiplicity, duplicate sources, builder ownership checks, deterministic local key allocation, primitive-owned diagnostics, and ordinary inspection, fingerprints, provenance, validation, compilation, and execution.
- Document each method classification clearly enough that aliases cannot be mistaken for modules and builder-only compositions cannot be mistaken for one durable semantic object.
- Add focused exact-lowering, identity, diagnostic, builder-parity, and bounded truth-table coverage.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No add_xor, add_level_gate, add_majority, or single keyed form that creates alias identity; callers use the existing explicit keyed primitive forms when durable node keys are required.
- No single keyed nand, nor, or xnor form and no hidden composition identity. Callers needing a durable boundary may author explicit primitives or wrap them in a user ModuleDef.
- No standard catalogue descriptor, StandardModuleRef, ModuleInstance, module hierarchy, module-level diagnostic, compatibility version, migration boundary, or privileged runtime path for any convenience.
- No debounce until InertialDelay is implemented.
- No any_pulse until Coalesce is implemented.
- No annotate_signal or other metadata-only Signal API.
- No low-enabled gate variants, convenience proliferation across polarity or priority permutations, pulse conveniences, stateful or temporal conveniences, new primitive kinds, persistence encoding, topology patches, or migration.

## Implementation obligations

- Reuse the existing NetworkBuilder primitive constructors and ModuleBuilder delegation pattern rather than adding parallel authored-graph or evaluator machinery.
- Preserve the exact convenience classification and exact primitive expansions from mossignal.authoring.level_conveniences.
- Collect each variadic input iterator once so majority derives its threshold from the same complete multiplicity-preserving input sequence passed to AtLeast.
- Ensure every signal-taking method returns AuthoringFailure::ForeignSignal for cross-builder inputs through the existing structured primitive-authoring path; do not partially author a multi-node builder-only operation before validating all supplied signals.
- Keep convenience names outside semantic identity. Equivalent fresh-builder convenience and direct-primitive constructions must yield the same authored structure and fingerprints when allocation state and metadata are equivalent.
- Preserve ordinary primitive diagnostics exactly, including empty, unary, duplicate-source, and constant-result findings; add no convenience-specific diagnostic codes or suppression.
- Keep production code free of unwrap and expect.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose direct method composition or a small private helper, favoring the simplest deterministic implementation that validates all inputs before mutating a multi-node composition.
- Choose the smallest iterator collection strategy for variadic conveniences; record and test the deterministic primitive and port allocation order without making it a new reusable product promise.
- Do not retain alias spelling as metadata unless existing APIs make that useful without changing semantic identity; omission is conforming.
- Test helpers may normalize only presentation and locally allocated key values when comparing convenience and explicit construction. They must retain node kind, configuration, incidence, multiplicity, diagnostics, hierarchy absence, and semantic fingerprints where equivalent identities are supplied.

## Expected change surface

- crates/mossignal/src/builder.rs for NetworkBuilder methods and ModuleBuilder parity.
- A focused integration test such as crates/mossignal/tests/level_conveniences.rs, plus only narrowly required existing regressions.
- Public rustdoc for the six methods and classifications.
- docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md only for the completion heading after accepted implementation.
- .beads when implementation is closed and synchronized.

## Required verification

1. Assert xor and xnor use exactly one binary Parity with stable two-port multiplicity; xnor adds exactly one downstream Not.
2. Assert level_gate uses exactly one binary All with value and enable both retained; no implicit polarity variant or simplification is introduced.
3. Assert majority uses exactly one AtLeast whose threshold is floor(arity / 2) + 1 for arities zero through at least five, preserves duplicate-source multiplicity, and handles empty input as AtLeast(1, []) with Low output and ordinary diagnostics.
4. Assert nand and nor author exactly All then Not and Any then Not for empty, unary, and multi-input cases without hidden simplification.
5. Exhaust bounded Level valuations for all six conveniences against independent Boolean laws, including duplicate-source cases and all empty and unary variadic boundaries.
6. Compare convenience-authored graphs with direct primitive authoring from equivalent fresh builder states: primitive kinds, configurations, port incidence, connections, diagnostics, output behavior, and NetworkFingerprint or ModuleFingerprint must agree after only permitted normalization.
7. Verify NetworkBuilder and ModuleBuilder expose equivalent methods, reject foreign signals structurally, retain no ModuleInstance or standard declaration, and execute solely through ordinary primitive machinery.
8. Verify direct graph inspection and provenance expose only canonical primitive subjects and relationships, with no convenience-owned subject, hierarchy, diagnostic, state, or pending work.
9. Verify existing primitive advisories remain exact for empty, unary, duplicate-source, and constant-result cases and no new diagnostic codes are introduced.
10. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then make check-dev. Final acceptance additionally runs make check-final.

## Blocking questions

None. Exact classifications, primitive expansions, total boundary behavior, and identity consequences are specified. Helper structure, allocation order within existing deterministic builder rules, and metadata retention remain bounded implementation freedom.

## Readiness

Ready. The governing mossignal.authoring.level_conveniences contract is independently reviewed, and no product or compatibility blocker prevents implementation.
notes: Implemented documented NetworkBuilder and ModuleBuilder xor, level_gate, majority, nand, nor, and xnor conveniences through the existing primitive authoring paths. Primitive aliases retain exactly one canonical primitive; builder-only operations retain only their exact ordinary primitive graphs. Added focused public-surface tests for exact authored structure and fingerprints, module parity, majority arities zero through five, complete binary and variadic boundary laws, ordinary diagnostics, foreign-signal failure before mutation, canonical primitive-only provenance, and absence of pending work. Corrective acceptance verification: cargo test -p mossignal --test level_conveniences (7 passed); make check-dev; make check-final.
close_reason: Implemented and accepted exact level aliases and builder-only conveniences on both typed builders

title: Validate and restore one machine snapshot
description:
## Objective and baseline

Implement roadmap item 54, `Snapshot validation and restoration`, from `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`.

Preparation baseline: `c4e7625a8a86d8d0491d81728d6f2ed5a247d6eb` (`ms-7ml: encode the canonical machine snapshot artifact`), on main, clean working tree before this preparation. Governing specifications were unchanged. The roadmap is sequencing context, not product authority. Items 32–53 stay done. Do not start item 55 or later. Do not mark item 54 done during preparation. Mark the roadmap heading when the implementation is in place.

Item 53 produced the `machine_snapshot` writer only. This bead is the strict reader and restorer for that artifact. Embed that encoding. Do not redesign the wire format, digest domains, or payload spelling.

The roadmap bullets for canonical-definition, fingerprint, module, and standard-expansion checks are satisfied against the caller-supplied `CompiledNetwork`, not by reading a definition or expansion out of the snapshot. The artifact still carries only `network_key`, `network_fingerprint`, and qualified state owners.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contract for this item

- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_restoration`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-restoration.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs hostile decode, canonical rejection, the version gate, identity and policy checks, refusal to migrate or repair, lifecycle and subject validation, events, episodes, provenance, settled-state and digest checks, standard-expansion checks, atomic publication, catalogue failures, and round-trip sufficiency.

Required facets: `decode-is-not-acceptance`, `hostile-and-bounded-decode`, `canonical-framing`, `integrity-and-version-gate`, `one-semantic-version-vector`, `identity-and-policy`, `no-migration-or-repair`, `lifecycle-subjects-and-state`, `uninitialized-state-is-declared`, `events-episodes-and-provenance`, `settled-state-and-digests`, `standard-expansion-check`, `atomic-publication`, `structured-failures`, and `round-trip-and-sufficiency`.

Apply recommendations `representative-decoder`, `nonexhaustive-failures`, and `bounded-fault-injection` by using those shapes. They are not additional product rules.

`known_uncovered` header-only inspection, forecast snapshots, policy rebinding, schema upgraders, historical corpora, replay logs, recovery tools, other artifact kinds, and long fuzz campaigns are outside this bead. The contract is reviewed. Do not demote it. If implementation discovers a specification-backed correction, leave that edit `draft` for independent review.

### Reviewed contracts reused without modification

- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_artifact`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-artifact.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: the bytes being validated. All cited sources were unchanged. Reuse `standalone-framing`, `envelope-and-kind`, `recorded-version-vector`, `snapshot-digest-identity`, `payload-identity`, `lifecycle-shape`, `state-and-pending-facts`, `required-observation`, `self-contained-provenance`, `history-and-metadata`, and `installed-topology-and-policy`. Do not reopen it. Its restoration `known_uncovered` is this bead.
- `mossignal.identity.machine_state_digests`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-state-digests.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: recompute execution and observable digests with the existing projections and compare them. Reuse `canonical-profile`, `domain-separated-construction`, `execution-projection`, `no-fabricated-uninitialized-facts`, `observable-extension`, `content-addressed-provenance`, `equality-is-not-validation`. Do not re-audit those rules.
- `mossignal.identity.time_domain`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/time-domain-identity.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: `TimeDomainId` is the 16-byte caller identity. Context, artifact, and compiled network must name the same one. Do not give `D` a persistence trait.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: ordinary restore requires the supplied policy's existing `RuntimePolicyId`. Do not rebind policy or re-encode limits.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: the snapshot fingerprint must equal the compiled network fingerprint. Do not build a second topology encoding.
- `mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: module identity stays inside the network fingerprint and the retained module definitions. Do not persist a second module artifact.
- `mossignal.standard.catalogue_foundation`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/standard-catalogue-foundation.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: `one-canonical-expanded-module` is what restoration regenerates and compares. Do not invent a second catalogue.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-lifecycle.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: restored uninitialized machines still have no fabricated ready facts. The installed revision is the snapshot revision, not a new spawn revision.
- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: preserve public `PendingEventKey` values and unordered equal-deadline batch semantics. Do not execute the calendar during restore.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.persistent_episodes`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/persistent-diagnostic-episodes.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: recompute episode identity from `stable-episode-identity`. That contract excludes restoration; the draft owns the check. Do not reopen it to delete `known_uncovered`.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: new persistence failures are catalogue `Problem` values. Do not add a string fallback.
- `mossignal.module.aware_execution`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/module-aware-execution.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: module-owned facts use qualified identity. Do not trust flat compiler keys.
- `mossignal.compile.compiled_network`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/compiled-network.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: reuse unchanged `immutable-topology-boundary`, `distinct-revision-local-dense-indices`, and `opaque-dense-private-surface`. `validated-identity-retention` and `deterministic-compilation` cite sources that have changed since review; those sections still carry the validated key, time domain, and fingerprints unchanged and still forbid dense layout from affecting persistence. The represented rules still hold. Do not reopen the contract. Restore is not a reason to edit it.
- `mossignal.identity.opening_fingerprint_projection`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/opening-fingerprint-projection.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: contextual only. Accepting the emitted version vector is not a fingerprint freeze and not a snapshot-format freeze.

Node contracts that still list snapshot restoration as `known_uncovered` stay unchanged. This contract represents restoration. Do not reopen them only to delete that note.

## Included scope

- Decode untrusted `machine_snapshot` bytes with an explicit `DecodePolicy` and a `PersistenceContext<D>`. Reject noncanonical, truncated, trailing, unknown, and over-limit input without panic or partial publication. Verify `SnapshotDigest` before semantic acceptance.
- Accept only the version vector the current encoder emits and the goldens lock. Reject every other component as `persistence.unsupported_version` with the component, versions, and no upgrader. Require the payload semantic components to equal the corresponding envelope components. Do not upgrade or migrate.
- Reject a recognized artifact kind other than `machine_snapshot` as `persistence.malformed_envelope`. Use `persistence.unknown_artifact_kind` only for an unrecognized kind string.
- `CompiledNetwork::restore(&self, snapshot, policy)` returns `Result<Machine<D>, RestoreFailure<D>>` only after the contract phase order succeeds. Borrow the network and take the snapshot and policy by value. Publish one complete machine or discard the candidate. Failure does not mutate the borrowed network or the caller's artifact bytes.
- Check time domain, network key, fingerprint, and exact runtime-policy identity. Validate lifecycle shape, stable subjects, signal kinds, state schemas, qualified module owners, pending events, the allocation cursor, episodes, and self-contained provenance. Accept a `pulse_delay_group` whose canonical payload is only the retained count. Do not require a provenance checkpoint record when the artifact claims no checkpoint authority. Recompute settled ready state with the existing reference evaluator and recompute all three digests.
- Before publication, re-resolve every standard declaration retained by the compiled network and reject an unavailable descriptor, interface mismatch, or expansion mismatch.
- Register the catalogue persistence codes this path can emit, with their specified severity, responsibility, delivery, and evidence families. Include the standard-module codes used for expansion failure.
- Prove semantic round trip from encode, decode, and restore, including uninitialized and ready machines, and prove the required rejection classes.

## Explicit exclusions

- No topology migration, key reassociation, state reset, semantic migration, or schema upgrader.
- No partial or best-effort recovery, silent repair, or `Low` fill for a missing level.
- No remote storage, file I/O, compression, streaming, encryption, or signatures.
- No replay frame, replay log, checkpoint bundle, definition artifact, or policy artifact. Sufficiency uses ordinary `apply` transactions, not a replay log and not history replay that reconstructs the snapshot.
- No `ForecastState::snapshot`, policy rebinding, or header-only inspection API.
- No second evaluator, second catalogue, or public `CauseDigest` type.
- No compatibility shim or freeze. The single accepted version vector is not a named baseline.
- Do not mark item 54 done during preparation. Mark the roadmap heading when the implementation is in place.

## Implementation freedom

The contract records these choices. Use them unless a simpler deterministic option still conforms. Test the choice and record it in the close-out. Do not amend specifications first.

- Reject a recognized non-snapshot artifact kind as `persistence.malformed_envelope`.
- Reject `persistence.topology_revision_mismatch` when a nested revision context is greater than the snapshot topology revision. Do not require originating revisions to be equal, and do not compare the revision with another machine.
- Map a duplicate or missing state-table owner to `persistence.state_schema_mismatch`. Map a lifecycle contradiction to `persistence.lifecycle_shape_invalid`. Do not invent a code.
- Success has no warning report.
- Keep canonical bytes, optional history, and metadata on the decoded artifact so re-encoding is byte-identical. Do not install them into the machine. A later snapshot of the restored machine may differ in `SnapshotDigest`.
- Rebuild private provenance from canonical records. Identity is the cause digest, not the old `CauseRef` integer.
- `DecodePolicy` takes every listed limit from the caller and has no hidden unbounded default. Enforce the limits a `machine_snapshot` can exceed. Do not decode other artifact kinds.
- Reuse the existing CBOR codec, digest functions, reference evaluator, and diagnostic registry. One shared checker may revalidate framing inside restore.
- Evidence structs may follow the current `ProblemEvidence` style. Private calendar storage may stay the existing representation.

## Expected change surface

`crates/mossignal/src/persistence.rs`, `compile.rs`, `diagnostics.rs`, `lib.rs`, and the machine construction path needed to publish a candidate without a public partial state. Restoration tests and the diagnostic golden inventory. Do not rewrite the snapshot payload spelling or the persistence specification to freeze it.

## Required verification

- Decode then re-encode of supported artifact bytes is identical, including a snapshot that carries optional history or metadata.
- Restore of an encoded uninitialized machine, a ready machine, every built-in state family this revision can own, pending temporal work, an active episode, and a module-qualified owner is semantically equivalent under the same compiled network, time domain, and policy. Compare semantic state, not private layout.
- The same later ordinary transactions on the original and restored machines agree in outputs, state, pending work, episodes, provenance roots, schedules, and both state digests.
- Rejection covers a bad prefix, truncation, trailing bytes, noncanonical encoding, integrity mismatch, a recognized non-snapshot kind, an unrecognized kind, an unsupported version component, payload semantic versions that disagree with the envelope, the wrong time domain, network, fingerprint, and policy, a lifecycle contradiction, an unknown subject, a state-schema or signal-kind mismatch, a non-future deadline, a bad event cursor, an invalid episode, each named provenance corruption, a tampered settled value with a recomputed envelope digest, a standard expansion mismatch, and a decode-limit excess. Each failure names its catalogue code and publishes no machine. A current encoder snapshot with no checkpoint record and a count-only pulse group restores.
- Restored public event keys and `next_pending_event_serial` match, and a later allocation does not reuse a key.
- A standard network whose retained expansion does not match the current descriptor is rejected before a machine exists.
- Run focused restoration tests while iterating, then `make check-dev` and `make check-final`. A long coverage-guided fuzz campaign is not an acceptance gate for this bead.

## Dependencies and readiness

Closed prerequisites are roadmap items 32–53, including the `machine_snapshot` encoder. No conflicting requirement, missing fundamental semantic, or explicit frozen compatibility promise blocks this slice.

The nested revision comparison and the catalogue code used for a duplicate state owner are implementation freedom. `AGENTS.md` records no snapshot-format freeze. A version label, golden, or the word "canonical" is not one.

Ready for implementation within the scope above.

title: Add LevelSetResetLatch and persistent diagnostic episodes
description:
## Objective and baseline

Implement roadmap item 44B, `LevelSetResetLatch` and persistent diagnostic episodes, from `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`. Extend the accepted 44A stored-level and diagnostic infrastructure with the level-controlled latch and the first machine-owned active episode lifecycle.

Preparation baseline: `cc3d74809c44dd9aab2bd27b662b600fe9abff65` on `main`, initially clean; governing specifications and existing contracts had no working-tree changes. Predecessor `ms-e43` is closed. No other open or active implementation bead exists at preparation time.

The roadmap is sequencing context. The contracts below preserve the authoritative specification basis. Keep the existing closed-node, full-topological, staged atomic transaction architecture.

## Contract basis

### Independently reviewed episode contract

- `mossignal.diagnostics.persistent_episodes` — `docs/specs/contracts/persistent-diagnostic-episodes.yaml` — **reviewed**. Required facets: `catalogue-safe-condition`, `stable-episode-identity`, `owned-active-and-change-records`, `continuous-condition-lifecycle`, `material-change-versus-reevaluation`, `candidate-owned-atomic-state`, `committed-ordered-publication`, `ready-inspection-and-causal-retention`, and `episode-conformance`.

### Reviewed contracts reused unchanged

- `mossignal.node.set_reset_latch_family` — `docs/specs/contracts/set-reset-latch-family.yaml`. Required facets: fixed shapes/shared policy, level-control law, exact conflict outcomes, occurrence-versus-episode delivery, previous/proposed state and immediate visibility, typed/dynamic/module authoring, validation/compilation/state, semantic identity, inspection/provenance/evidence, and latch conformance. Its general episode-representation exclusion is covered by the new contract; its snapshot and migration facets remain outside this task.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model` — `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`. Reuse authoritative registry, fixed classification, safe valid combinations, exact typed evidence, structured comparison, registry conformance, and golden catalogue.
- `mossignal.runtime.stateful_reaction_foundation` — `docs/specs/contracts/stateful-reaction-foundation.yaml`. Reuse previous/proposed state, current-output causality, declared initialization, atomic successor commit, family storage, inspection, and verification.
- `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction` — `docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml` and `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction` — `docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml`. Reuse ordinary settlement, exact input/lifecycle boundaries, complete candidate publication, resolvable causes, runtime budgets, and failure preservation.
- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`. Reuse chronological ready advancement, equal-deadline batches, direct-jump equivalence, schedule/result ordering, and single outer-transaction publication.
- `mossignal.module.aware_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/module-aware-execution.yaml`. Reuse ordinary primitive lowering, independent qualified owners, retained hierarchy, module-transparent settlement/atomicity/budgets, and qualified provenance/observation.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.runtime_occurrences` — `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-diagnostic-occurrences.yaml`. Preserve the existing result-owned transient occurrence path and its distinction from active episode state.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint` — `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`. Reuse deterministic semantic identity, parameter/role sensitivity, representation exclusions, golden verification, and pre-stability projection policy.
- `mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint` — `docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml`. Reuse `complete-user-module-projection`, `representation-and-instance-exclusions`, and `deterministic-and-sensitive-identity` for the already-required module fingerprint integration and verification.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy` — `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`. Reuse existing semantic limits, atomic budget failure, and implemented budget boundary tests; this task adds no policy family.
- `mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder` — `docs/specs/contracts/typed-network-builder.yaml` and `mossignal.authoring.typed_module_builder` — `docs/specs/contracts/typed-module-builder.yaml`. Reuse builder-scoped signals, exact explicit identities, primitive family parity, canonical lowering, and ordinary validation completion.
- `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_dependency_graph` — `docs/specs/contracts/current-reaction-dependency-graph.yaml`. Reuse only `conservative-static-signatures`, whose cited sources are unchanged; latch-specific signatures and verification come from the latch contract. The older contract's changed compilation-verification citation is not used for this bead.

All reused facets above have unchanged reviewed source evidence. Independent review promoted the new persistent-episodes contract with exact reviewed source hashes; existing reviewed contracts remain unchanged. The module-fingerprint contract explicitly owns the existing module-identity verification obligation.

## Included scope

### Level-controlled latch

- Add `LevelSetResetConfig` with explicit initial `LogicLevel` and the existing `ConflictPolicy`; add the closed `LevelSetResetLatch` node with fixed Level set/reset inputs and one Level output.
- Provide typed `level_set_reset_latch`, explicit-keyed `add_level_set_reset_latch`, and dynamic construction on the existing network/module paths. Carry exact roles and kinds through the central node schema, malformed-definition validation, reaction dependencies/cycles, compilation, and fingerprints.
- Read fully settled current controls and previous stored state: High/Low sets High, Low/High resets Low, Low/Low retains, and High/High applies policy. Expose the current output downstream immediately and commit one proposed successor only on success.
- Reuse the accepted shared stored-level value/proposed-state family for Toggle and PulseSetResetLatch. Do not add a parallel Level-latch Boolean value vector. This is a task-specific implementation choice building on 44A, not a new permanent storage promise.
- Preserve the four policy outcomes. Dominant policies choose their specified level; RetainAndDiagnose retains state and updates the persistent episode; RejectTransaction returns the exact structured rejection and publishes nothing.

### Episode identities, records, and catalogue integration

- Introduce `ProblemDelivery::PersistentEpisode`, opaque `DiagnosticConditionKey` and `DiagnosticEpisodeId`, owned `ActiveDiagnosticEpisode<D>`, and owned `DiagnosticEpisodeChange<D>` with the specified change-kind distinction. Include the `Terminated` vocabulary, but defer any topology-removal producer until topology replacement exists.
- Use `runtime.level_latch_conflict_retained` as Warning/Advisory/PersistentEpisode and `runtime.level_latch_conflict_rejected` as Error/SemanticRejection/OperationFailure. Both use the ConflictEvidence family with exact code/evidence association in the existing authoritative registry.
- Generalize the current pulse-specific ConflictEvidence representation to express settled Level controls as well as complete Pulse counts without confusing the two. Retain stable direct or module-qualified owner, conflict policy, previous stored level, exact logical time, and revision. Preserve the pulse codes and occurrence semantics.
- Derive the condition key from code, primary owning subject, and the code-defined discriminator; derive episode identity from network identity plus that semantic condition. Do not use presentation metadata, dense slots, or provenance arena IDs. Separate module instances with equal local node keys must have separate qualified episode owners.
- Safe construction must reject unsupported delivery, code/evidence mismatches, and disagreement between an active record's key and current Problem. Reuse the common diagnostic kernel and update catalogue/failure inventories for the implemented leaves.

### Candidate lifecycle, results, and inspection

- Maintain machine-owned active episodes inside candidate state. On initialization or a later reaction, establish Began for a newly active retained conflict, preserve an unchanged active episode without repeated publication, and publish Changed for material evidence changes.
- When the conflict ends, remove its active state and publish Resolved. The general contract permits resolution events; this bead selects their publication as requested by 44B. A later new conflict begins again with the correct new begin time under the stable identity rule.
- Reconcile episodes at every processed logical reaction, including internal PulseDelay deadlines. Accumulate chronological episode changes in the one successful owned transaction result; begin and resolve within the same outer transaction must both survive in the result even if no episode remains active at its end.
- Publish the diagnostic-episode part of semantic changes through structured owned result access. A bounded `SemanticChangeSet` or equivalent accessor projection may fit the existing result API; do not implement absent result families merely to fill the specification's eventual complete shape.
- Expose deterministic owned active-episode inspection, returning the existing structured not-initialized category before Ready. Provide focused level-latch definition/current inspection, including declared versus committed level, policy, settled controls/output, and applicable state cause. Keep module-qualified inspection coherent.
- Preserve required provenance for latch output/state and causally relevant episode evidence. Retained result causes must remain resolvable after later machine transactions. Current support and latest stored-state establishment must remain distinct where their meanings differ.
- Apply existing event/provenance budget accounting to the added publication work. Any rejection after candidate episode, stored-state, output, scheduling, or provenance work preserves the complete published machine and every earlier retained result.

## Implementation obligations and freedom

- Keep concrete enums and the ordinary evaluator/transaction path; no callback evaluator, general automaton framework, plugin registry, or new crate. Production code remains free of unwrap/expect. Document deliberate public types and add SPEC traces only for non-obvious enforced rules.
- Choose the simplest deterministic representation for condition discriminators, network/condition episode identity encoding, active episode maps, stable ordering among same-time subjects, and transition staging. Test and record the chosen representation; there is no release freeze or historical encoding support to preserve.
- The initial retained level-conflict has one condition per owning latch. The discriminator's exact encoding is bounded implementation freedom; record it in the registry/implementation and test that changing evidence does not accidentally create a new condition identity.
- Define materiality over the condition's meaningful evidence, not full Problem equality including reevaluation time. Unrelated later transactions must neither emit Changed nor reset begin/material-change timestamps. Choose and test a deterministic current-evidence refresh policy that preserves exact event evidence and causal ownership.
- Choose and test the simplest coherent before/after payload convention for lifecycle changes. Materially changed evidence can be exercised through a focused internal episode-transition test using valid catalogue-backed Problems when an immutable level latch cannot naturally produce that transition during a continuous conflict. Do not invent a production node or topology API solely to produce a test case.
- Preserve 44A's accepted stored-state cause convention where applicable; any required node-specific refinement must be deterministic, tested, and recorded. Private helper/type names and accessor shapes remain flexible within the specified owned distinctions.
- Reuse existing condition-discriminator and exact-evidence machinery where applicable. Cross-reaction material change is a lifecycle update, not contradictory same-detection evidence merging. No general diagnostic-collection refactor is required.

## Required verification

1. Exhaust the 32 core cases: two previous stored levels × four settled set/reset combinations × four policies. Cover initialization and multi-reaction set/reset/retain/conflict histories, including same-value requests.
2. Verify typed, explicit-keyed, dynamic, and module construction equivalence; fixed-role/kind errors; foreign signals and duplicate identity rejection; conservative dependency/cycle behavior; deterministic compiled storage correspondence and kind/role/configuration-sensitive network/module fingerprints.
3. Verify same-reaction LevelSetResetLatch → AnyEdge propagation and controls that themselves settle through upstream stateful/level nodes. Permute authored connection/input order to expose accidental control ordering.
4. Verify shared stored-level storage and unchanged Toggle/PulseSetResetLatch behavior with mixed consumers, including inspection and retained causes.
5. Verify preinitialization episode inspection failure; empty active state after non-conflicting initialization; Began during conflicting initialization; exact record fields, classification, evidence, begin/material-change timestamps, and owning identity.
6. Verify unchanged continuation across unrelated and explicitly repeated equal-control transactions; material change through the bounded transition model; Resolved; and a later new Began. Compare structured before/after payloads and the recorded materiality/identity conventions.
7. Verify distinct direct/module/nested-module subjects, multiple simultaneous conflicts, deterministic same-time ordering, and identity invariance under insertion/private-slot/provenance-layout changes. Do not normalize away public episode identity.
8. Use existing PulseDelay plus stored-level primitives to exercise episode begin/resolution at internal deadlines and requested-time reactions; verify actual timestamps and direct-jump versus stepwise equivalence of final state and accumulated change streams.
9. Verify complete rollback after candidate episode creation, material update, or resolution, including an outer transaction that processes earlier deadlines then fails. Exercise existing rejection/budget paths and bounded internal staging tests where needed; compare active episodes, lifecycle/time/revision, external valuation, stored levels/causes, pending events/cursors, outputs/baselines, schedule, and provenance.
10. Verify safe delivery and code/evidence/key agreement; exact retained/rejected level-conflict leaves; pulse-occurrence separation; code-specific discriminator and applicable merge rules; catalogue/failure inventory goldens.
11. Verify owned inspection/results remain meaningful after subsequent transactions, causally relevant evidence remains explainable, and any exposed result CauseRef resolves through its immutable view. Cover added budget accounting below/at/above the boundary where representable.
12. Run focused latch, episode, Toggle, edge, module, temporal, diagnostic, provenance, and transaction tests; then `make check-dev`. Final acceptance additionally requires `make check-final` under the repository testing policy.

## Exclusions and known later integration

- No SampleHold, resettable standard modules, counters, general state machines, or new temporal primitive.
- No snapshot/restore/replay/digest implementation, topology patches, state migration, policy-change migration, subject reassociation, or termination producer. The contracts' obligations for those systems remain later integration work, not waived semantics.
- No observers, subscriptions, host delivery, logging, rendering, retained completed-episode history, general explanation-query engine, or broad SemanticChangeSet completion.
- No evaluator/calendar optimization, repository-wide refactor, specification amendment, contract promotion, compatibility shim, historical reader, or release-readiness freeze.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/{authored,builder,node_schema,lib}.rs` and the existing module-authoring path for closed kind/configuration, exact ports, typed construction, and exports.
- `crates/mossignal/src/{validation,compile,machine,transaction,identity}.rs` for schema use, shared stored-level descriptors, level evaluation, episode candidate ownership, result publication, inspection, provenance, and identity.
- `crates/mossignal/src/diagnostics.rs` and, if useful, one private episode module for safe owned records, catalogue/evidence integration, deterministic identity, and lifecycle helpers.
- Focused integration/unit tests and existing diagnostic/failure inventory goldens. Mark roadmap 44B DONE only after implementation; preserve the existing closed predecessor bead.

## Task-scoped research disposition

Latch shapes/laws, authoring, validation/compilation, inspection/provenance, fingerprints, conflict codes, and finite conformance map to the unchanged latch contract. Atomic state, chronology, modules, diagnostics, budgets, and typed lowering reuse the reviewed facets listed above. Episode key/ID, safe owned records, lifecycle/materiality, committed publication, Ready-only inspection, relevant causal retention, and distinct episode tests map to the new persistent-episodes contract. Snapshot/replay/digests and reconfiguration/termination sources were inspected only to identify the explicit later integration boundary. No product requirement was inferred from the roadmap or existing pulse-specific private representation.

## Blocking questions and readiness

No unresolved product blocker. Representation, discriminator/identity encoding, materiality details consistent with warning suppression, result accessors, and bounded transition-test design are implementation freedom with a deterministic implementation-and-test path.

Independently reviewed, open, bounded, and ready for implementation. The persistent-episodes contract is reviewed with all cited sources unchanged. Review added the unchanged module-fingerprint contract as the explicit owner of the existing module-identity obligation; it did not expand the task. The only implementation predecessor is closed `ms-e43`.
acceptance_criteria: Implement roadmap 44B over the accepted shared stored-level family: complete LevelSetResetLatch authoring, schema, validation, compilation, state/output, inspection, provenance, and fingerprint integration; catalogue-safe level-conflict evidence and rejection; stable condition/episode identities and owned active/change records; deterministic Began/Changed/Resolved publication with unchanged-warning suppression and active inspection; chronological outer-transaction rollback including episode state and required provenance; focused exhaustive and lifecycle conformance; updated diagnostic/failure inventories; make check-dev passing, and make check-final at final acceptance. Independent review of the persistent-episodes contract and bounded bead is complete; reuse their reviewed baseline during implementation.
notes:
Implemented roadmap 44B on the independently reviewed planning baseline 1b3a7e5. No specification or contract changes were required during implementation.

Concrete implementation choices:
- LevelSetResetLatch reuses the Toggle/PulseSetResetLatch stored-level value vector. Both latch kinds share a private state-cause map while retaining their own control laws. Initialization and explicit set/reset requests establish a stored-state cause even when the requested value equals the previous value; retain preserves the earlier establishment. Current reaction support is separate.
- The retained-level-conflict condition has singleton discriminator 0 per stable owner. Episode IDs use domain-separated BLAKE3 over NetworkKey, catalogue code, tagged direct or fully qualified owner, and discriminator. Dense slots, fingerprints, presentation, timestamps, and cause IDs do not participate. A later active interval reuses the semantic condition ID with a new begin time.
- Candidate episodes use a stable owner-ordered BTreeMap. Materiality compares owner, policy, previous level, typed controls, and revision; reevaluation time alone is immaterial. Unchanged episodes retain the last material Problem, timestamps, and immutable causal view.
- Owned lifecycle changes use absent/present before/after payloads for Began, present/present for Changed, and present/absent for Resolved. TransactionResult exposes the bounded diagnostic_episode_changes projection in chronological/stable-owner order. Each change cause resolves through its result; active inspection retains its own immutable provenance view. Terminated is vocabulary only until topology replacement exists.
- ConflictEvidence now distinguishes exact Pulse counts from exact Level controls. Catalogue-safe episode construction and pulse occurrence construction enforce the corresponding kind. Episode publications count toward existing event budgets.

Verification before independent acceptance: 208 library tests and 12 new LevelSetResetLatch integration tests pass, covering the 32 control/state/policy laws at initialization and Ready, lifecycle/materiality, nested modules, identity and fingerprints, same-reaction edges, internal deadlines, budgets, and complete transaction rollback. A regression first reproduced that pulse occurrence construction accepted Level evidence after generalizing ConflictEvidence; the kind guard now rejects it. The new fingerprint golden was derived from the existing canonical projection with explicit Level kind and port-order changes. Final acceptance verification is recorded below.

Independent corrective implementation acceptance:
- Reviewed the complete proposal against the closed bead and unchanged reviewed contract basis. No new contract, specification amendment, compatibility baseline, or expanded implementation scope was required. The Level latch uses the ordinary typed/dynamic/module lowering, schema, shared stored-level evaluator, and atomic publication paths; deferred persistence, topology replacement, and observers remain excluded.
- Corrected a concrete condition-identity defect. The original DiagnosticConditionKey derived equality/order over a Problem primary NodeKey allocated by private module flattening. A focused regression first failed with the same qualified module latch represented by private NodeKey(0) versus NodeKey(1) after adding an unrelated containing node. Removed that redundant field and its accessor from the newly introduced key: equality and ordering now use stable direct/fully qualified owner, catalogue code, and singleton discriminator only. The owner accessor provides its structural subject; episode ID encoding is unchanged. The permanent regression verifies equal condition keys and episode IDs across the allocation change.
- Strengthened verification with an independently initialized exhaustive 32-case Ready matrix, exact latest state-establishment transaction-time assertions for set/reset, same-value requests, and retention, and a mixed direct/two-module test proving that resolving one instance changes neither the remaining active evidence nor independent stored values. The Level latch integration suite now has 15 tests. Existing bounded episode tests cover material Changed and discarded candidate state; transaction tests compare the complete published machine after failures following earlier internal creation or resolution.
- Final corrected-state verification passed: cargo test -q -p mossignal --test level_set_reset_latch --lib (208 library tests and 15 Level latch integration tests), git diff --check, make check-dev, and make check-final. The final gate includes all workspace tests, contract-tool tests, compilation, formatting, static guardrails, clippy without warnings, doctests, documentation, and dependency policy. Earlier pre-correction gate passes were superseded by these corrected-state passes.
- Bead ms-6af remained closed throughout review; predecessor ms-e43 is closed and dependencies are coherent. Roadmap 44B is DONE. Accepted implementation, tests, goldens, roadmap, and synchronized closed bead record are one commit; no push is authorized.
close_reason: Implemented LevelSetResetLatch and candidate-owned persistent diagnostic episodes with deterministic identities, lifecycle publication, exact evidence, inspection/provenance, and atomic chronological rollback. Focused conformance and make check-dev pass; the closed proposal is ready for independent corrective acceptance.
