title: Implement level InputDelta and builder
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 19: add the owned level-only InputDelta<D> artifact and ordinary current-topology InputDeltaBuilder<D>. Bind each completed delta to the exact compiled network and input schema, retain only explicitly supplied external level observations, and preserve omission as later retention of the ready machines prior authoritative value. Stop before transaction execution.

## Contract basis

- `mossignal.runtime.level_input_delta`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/level-input-delta.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs the owned opaque delta, current-topology builder, identity binding, explicit observations, omission semantics, deterministic construction, invalid-observation rejection, and lifecycle relationship.
- `mossignal.identity.input_schema_fingerprint`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/input-schema-fingerprint.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged
  - required facet: `future-input-binding` keeps schema identity distinct from network identity and binds observations by stable endpoint identity.
- `mossignal.compile.compiled_network`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/compiled-network.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged
  - required facets: `immutable-topology-boundary`, `validated-identity-retention`, and `opaque-dense-private-surface` supply the exact immutable builder context without exposing dense layout.
- `mossignal.runtime.level_input_snapshot`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/level-input-snapshot.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged as contextual established pattern
  - required facet: snapshots and deltas share owned exact-bound artifact conventions but remain distinct, non-interchangeable public types.

The delta contract intentionally leaves prepared-patch target deltas in `known_uncovered`; no target revision, establish obligation, or removed-input behavior is required here.

## Included scope

- Add public opaque `InputDelta<D>` and `InputDeltaBuilder<D>` types for the restricted level-only model.
- Add `CompiledNetwork<D>::input_delta()` as the ordinary builder origin for the exact current compiled topology.
- Retain the exact NetworkKey, NetworkFingerprint, and InputSchemaFingerprint separately in each completed delta.
- Add explicit `set(ExternalInputKey<Level>, LogicLevel)` construction for existing external level inputs.
- Permit empty, partial, and complete deltas; omission records no replacement value and will mean retention when later ready-machine execution consumes the artifact.
- Permit explicit reassertion of either level value.
- Reject an endpoint outside the bound external level-input schema.
- Reject repeated observations for one endpoint and preserve the existing structured distinction between an equivalent duplicate and a conflicting value.
- Preserve equivalent semantic behavior independent of builder insertion order without promising a public iteration order.
- Export the deliberate public types and document the identity, lifecycle, and omission boundaries.

## Explicit exclusions and non-goals

- No `Transaction::advance`, ready-machine `Machine::apply`, time advancement, evaluator invocation, external-level mutation, output events, provenance, staging, rollback, or lifecycle rejection implementation.
- No pulse observations, PulseCount storage, pulse input builder method, or pulse transaction integration.
- No prepared patch, target schema, `establish`, newly introduced or removed endpoint behavior, target revision binding, reconfiguration, or topology migration.
- No binding projection, caller-object-model interpretation, ambiguous observations, or ergonomic bound-machine facade.
- No persistence artifact encoding or decoding, replay, restoration, forecast, state digests, or serialization derives.
- Do not merge InputSnapshot and InputDelta or make them interchangeable.
- Do not change reviewed contracts unless implementation discovers a reusable specification-backed correction; any changed contract remains draft and requires independent review.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement `compiled-builder-origin`, `owned-opaque-network-bound-artifact`, `exact-current-schema-binding`, `explicit-level-observations`, `omission-means-retention`, `rejects-invalid-observations`, and `deterministic-unordered-batch` from `mossignal.runtime.level_input_delta` within this beads restricted construction boundary.
- Obtain identity and endpoint membership from CompiledNetwork rather than accepting caller-supplied identity tokens or collection positions.
- Reuse or deliberately extend the existing InputBuildFailure family so unknown, duplicate, and conflicting observations remain structured and comparable; do not add unreachable failure variants merely for future systems.
- Keep snapshot completeness behavior unchanged. InputDelta::finish must not require omitted existing levels or infer them as Low.
- Keep dense compiled indices, authored insertion order, and diagnostic metadata from affecting delta semantics.
- Preserve generic trait behavior without adding unrelated bounds on D.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Private storage, module placement, accessor details, helper names, and whether snapshot and delta builders share private helpers are free when the public artifact boundaries remain distinct.
- Choose the simplest deterministic stable-keyed representation, test insertion-order-independent semantic behavior, and record the concrete choice in the implementation close-out without making iteration order or a particular equality implementation a permanent public promise.
- The current-topology builder need not expose `establish` or a caller-supplied NetworkRevision. Exact machine revision belongs to the later transaction, while target revision context belongs to future prepared-patch deltas.
- Derives beyond the semantic and testing needs of this slice are implementation choices; do not add persistence or broad compatibility promises.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/input.rs` for the delta artifact, builder, construction failures, and focused tests.
- `crates/mossignal/src/compile.rs` for the builder entry point and exact schema membership.
- `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs` for deliberate exports.
- `docs/specs/contracts/level-input-delta.yaml` only for implementation-discovered reusable specification-backed corrections; any later change requires independent review.
- `.beads/` when implementation acceptance closes and synchronizes the bead.

## Required verification

1. Build empty, single-input, partial, complete, and explicit reassertion deltas and verify exact network and schema identity retention.
2. Verify omission remains absence from the delta rather than an inferred Low or a finish-time completeness error.
3. Verify unknown external level inputs fail structurally.
4. Verify repeated equal observations report duplicate input and repeated unequal observations report conflict, preserving the first and second values where represented.
5. Build equivalent deltas through different insertion orders and verify equivalent semantic observations without requiring a public iteration-order guarantee.
6. Verify deltas from networks with foreign network identity or schema remain distinguishable and cannot be positionally rebound.
7. Verify InputSnapshot completeness and construction behavior remain unchanged and the two artifacts are distinct public types.
8. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`; final acceptance additionally runs `make check-final`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The restricted CompiledNetwork creates owned level-only delta builders bound to its exact stable identities and endpoint schema.
- Completed deltas retain exactly the explicit valid observations, permit omission without defaulting or completeness rejection, and remain deterministic across construction order.
- Unknown, duplicate, and conflicting observations produce structured failures without corrupting the builder boundary or altering snapshot behavior.
- No transaction execution, pulse, patch, projection, or persistence subsystem is introduced.
- Focused verification and both repository gates pass.

## Dependencies and readiness

Roadmap item 18 (`ms-miv`) is closed and accepted. Reviewed compilation, identity, and snapshot contracts are unchanged. The delta contract is reviewed, and no conflicting requirement, missing fundamental semantic rule, or frozen compatibility promise blocks this bounded implementation slice. The bead is open, unblocked, and implementation-ready.
notes:
Implementation close-out:
- Added distinct owned opaque InputDelta<D> and InputDeltaBuilder<D> public types.
- Added CompiledNetwork<D>::input_delta() bound to the exact NetworkKey, NetworkFingerprint, InputSchemaFingerprint, and stable typed external level-input schema.
- Delta construction accepts empty, partial, complete, and explicit reassertion batches; omitted inputs remain absent rather than becoming Low or causing completeness failure.
- Reused InputBuildFailure for structured unknown, duplicate-equivalent, and conflicting observations.
- Chose private BTreeSet membership and BTreeMap observation storage for simple deterministic stable-key semantics without promising public iteration order.
- Preserved InputSnapshot completeness behavior and stopped before transaction execution, pulse, patch, projection, or persistence work.

Verification:
- Focused input tests: passed (6 tests)
- make check-dev: passed
- make check-final: passed
close_reason: Implemented and verified level InputDelta construction.

title: Implement first variadic primitive: All
description:

- Do not replace the existing unchecked graph, validation-report model, dependency graph, compiler, or full evaluator.
- Do not add a successor fingerprint domain, historical reader, upgrader, migration path, or compatibility implementation.

## Implementation obligations

- Honor `total-commutative-port-law`, `stable-port-multiplicity`, `typed-and-dynamic-authoring`, `causality-and-execution`, `nonblocking-variadic-quality-findings`, `variadic-all-conformance`, and `canonical-fingerprint-boundary` from `mossignal.node.variadic_all`.

2. Verify repeated one-source-to-many-ports multiplicity, the specified duplicate-source advisory behavior, and behavior under variadic port permutations with stable identities retained.

4. Verify zero and unary All forms retain a valid artifact alongside their canonical non-blocking diagnostics.
5. Verify foreign builder signals and immediately determinable duplicate explicit node/port keys are structured authoring failures.
6. Verify the exact v1 All canonical node-kind variant, port-sensitive fingerprinting, permutation invariance, and a hand-reviewed golden vector.

## Resolved planning decision

Fingerprint-domain version 1 remains a development projection until an explicit stabilization baseline. This bead extends v1 with the authoritative `["all", null]` variant and synchronizes its golden fixtures without adding compatibility machinery.

## Expected change surface

- authoritative fingerprint specification and verification policy
- affected draft contracts and `.beads/` state

## Dependencies

## Readiness

Implemented proposal is ready for corrective acceptance under the accepted pre-stability fingerprint policy. Changed contracts have been independently reviewed and promoted.
notes:

title: Implement problem and report kernel
description:
# Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 7 as the durable common problem-reporting architecture consumed by the opening authored-graph and structural-validation tasks. Do not introduce a temporary diagnostic or identity model.

## Contract basis

All four governing records are reviewed and accepted for reuse at their recorded evidence baselines:

- `mossignal.diagnostics.subject_references`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-subject-references.yaml`
  - role: stable diagnostic subject identity, related-subject roles, and canonical ordering for the seven initial variants
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`
  - role: catalogue registry, codes, classifications, typed evidence, `Problem<D>`, and `Diagnostic<D>`
- `mossignal.diagnostics.collections`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-collections.yaml`
  - role: `DiagnosticSet<D>`, canonical ordering, condition identity, deduplication, and evidence merging for the opening slice
- `mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/artifact-reports.yaml`
  - role: `Report<T, D>`, artifact blocking semantics, and complete diagnostic retention

## Included scope

- Implement the durable catalogue-backed diagnostic kernel.
- Implement the specified `Severity` and `Responsibility` families with code-fixed lookup.
- Implement `Problem<D>`, typed code-specific `ProblemEvidence<D>`, related subjects, safe suggestions, and the ReportFinding-only `Diagnostic<D>` wrapper.
- Implement `SubjectRef` support needed by this slice for `Network`, `Node`, `InPort`, `OutPort`, `Connection`, `ExternalInput`, and `ExternalOutput`, including their permanent comparison tags and canonical payload order.
- Implement only these opening structural-validation codes: `validation.duplicate_key`, `validation.missing_node`, `validation.missing_port`, `validation.missing_endpoint`, `validation.invalid_direction`, `validation.signal_kind_mismatch`, `validation.unsupported_multiple_drivers`, `validation.missing_required_input`, and `validation.invalid_fixed_arity`.
- Implement `DiagnosticSet<D>` with canonical iteration, condition-key deduplication, and the specified exact-agreement, set-union, and duplicate-claim multiset behavior.
- Implement `Report<T, D>` and `ReportFailure<D>` with complete diagnostic retention and blocking-artifact behavior.
- Use one authoritative declarative registry for every implemented code; do not maintain parallel code, evidence, classification, delivery, discriminator, or merge tables.

## Explicit exclusions

- `SubjectRef` variants and payload comparison outside the seven initial variants.
- Exhaustive catalogue implementation beyond the nine opening validation codes.
- Module-binding, reassociation, and module-interface diagnostic identity contexts.
- Authored graph storage and structural validation detector logic.
- Runtime diagnostic occurrences.
- Persistent diagnostic episodes.
- Internal-defect delivery infrastructure beyond the representation needed for `internal.diagnostic_evidence_conflict`.
- Provenance, rendering, localization, logging, observer delivery, persistence encoding, serialization, and schema decoding.
- Any operation for combining two `Report` values or resolving two produced artifacts.
- Rust compatibility shims or a second temporary problem representation.

These exclusions correspond to adjacent or `known_uncovered` contract facets and do not block this bead.

## Implementation freedom

- Private enum and struct names, role and category variant spelling, storage layout, helper types, construction APIs, comparison keys, and merge algorithms remain implementation choices when the specified distinctions and deterministic behavior are preserved.
- A private diagnostic projection may preserve authored facts needed by evidence without exposing complete authored record storage shapes.
- Canonical subject comparison may use a private comparator or ordering key; no public `Ord` implementation is required by this bead.
- Implementation may create or extend draft contracts when it discovers reusable specification-backed knowledge already determined by the specifications and this bead. Such drafts require independent review before final acceptance and do not authorize scope expansion.

## Expected change surface

- A diagnostics-focused module or small module family under `crates/mossignal/src/`.
- Public module integration in `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs`.
- Focused unit and compile-boundary documentation tests colocated with the implementation.
- No unrelated changes to signal, time, key, or metadata semantics.

## Required verification

- Registry coverage and exact fixed severity, responsibility, delivery, evidence association, primary-subject rule, discriminator, and merge law for every implemented code.
- Safe APIs cannot construct code/evidence, classification, or delivery mismatches.
- Structured comparison excludes rendered prose.
- Stable ordering across the seven initial `SubjectRef` variants, with tag comparison before payload comparison and `Level` before `Pulse` for erased signal-bearing keys.
- Permutations of discovery and unordered evidence produce identical `DiagnosticSet` values and iteration order.
- Duplicate-key evidence is independent of discovery order, symmetric, complete, canonically ordered, and retains meaningful claim multiplicity without multiplying repeated detection.
- Deduplication covers repeated equal exact-agreement evidence, distinct subjects, distinct discriminators, partial conflicting-driver set union, partial fixed-arity port-set union, and contradictory exact-agreement evidence.
- Contradictory exact-agreement evidence produces `internal.diagnostic_evidence_conflict`.
- Report tests cover blocking artifact absence, non-blocking artifact presence, complete `ReportFailure` diagnostics, and accumulation of unrelated safe findings.
- Run focused tests while iterating, then `make check-dev` and `make check-final`.

## Blocking open questions

None.

## Readiness

Open and claimable. The required stable key families already exist, the represented opening semantics are reviewed, and this bead has no dependency on the contracts' known-uncovered future facets.
close_reason: Corrected diagnostic condition identity, merging, conflict retention, and regression coverage

title: Implement restricted full topological evaluator
description:
## Objective

Implement the restricted level-only Constant/Not full reference evaluator over CompiledNetwork<D>: accept external level facts and evaluate every reaction operation once in the retained deterministic topological order.

## Contract basis

- mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator
  - docs/specs/contracts/restricted-full-topological-evaluator.yaml
  - status: reviewed
  - role: reference-evaluator boundary, root facts, settlement order, Constant/Not laws, and direct verification.

- mossignal.compile.compiled_network
  - docs/specs/contracts/compiled-network.yaml
  - status: reviewed, used unchanged
  - role: immutable compiled topology, private dense execution metadata, and retained deterministic operation order.

- mossignal.graph.current_reaction_dependency_graph
  - docs/specs/contracts/current-reaction-dependency-graph.yaml
  - status: reviewed, used unchanged
  - role: stable-subject reaction relation, external input root facts, and output observation.

- mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition
  - docs/specs/contracts/authored-network-definition.yaml
  - status: reviewed, used unchanged
  - role: restricted authored Constant/Not and external-boundary structure behind validated compilation.

## Included scope

- Implement one full reference evaluator for the existing immutable restricted compiled topology.
- Accept caller-supplied external level facts keyed by represented external level inputs.
- Traverse the retained deterministic topological order exactly once, only after predecessors have settled.
- Evaluate Constant and Not, propagate node outputs, and observe external outputs.
- Add focused direct tests for node laws, multi-node chains, external inputs and outputs, exact-once execution, and predecessor availability.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- Do not implement Machine, initialization, lifecycle, transactions, cloning or staging, atomic publication, snapshots, deltas, input-completeness validation, runtime policy, or public runtime APIs.
- Do not implement pulse values, stateful or temporal nodes, events, dirty propagation, incremental evaluation, worklists, diagnostics, provenance, persistence, replay, graph-query APIs, or topology patches.
- Do not expose compiled dense indices, adjacency, arenas, or worklists publicly.
- Do not change validation, cycle analysis, fingerprint construction, or compiled topology semantics.

## Implementation obligations

- Evaluate only the immutable compiled Constant/Not topology and introduce no mutable machine state.
- Treat represented external level inputs as caller-provided root facts; external outputs observe their authored source without transformation.
- Evaluate every represented reaction operation exactly once in the compiled deterministic topological order, after all affected predecessor results are final.
- Apply the exact restricted node laws: Constant yields its configured LogicLevel; Not yields the logical complement of its one settled level input.
- Keep the evaluator clear and deterministic. It is the future correctness oracle for optimized incremental execution.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- The evaluator/result interface may remain crate-private or test-oriented; this task does not establish a general public runtime API.
- Choose the simplest deterministic input/result storage and error-free internal shape compatible with the already validated compiled topology.
- It may retain intermediate settled results for direct test inspection, but the specifications do not require a particular result interface.
- Input snapshot completeness, unknown-input rejection, duplicate-observation rules, and public builders are expressly deferred to roadmap item 15.
- Prefer direct auditable traversal over caching or allocation optimization; record and test any ordinary representation choice during implementation.

## Expected change surface

- crates/mossignal/src/compile.rs or a focused private evaluator module
- crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs only if a deliberate minimal test-facing internal boundary requires it
- focused unit tests adjacent to the evaluator
- docs/specs/contracts/restricted-full-topological-evaluator.yaml only for implementation-discovered reusable facts; any change remains draft
- .beads/ when implementation acceptance closes the bead

## Required verification

1. Directly test Constant High and Low and both Not input values against their node laws.
2. Test a hand-authored multi-node chain and its expected settled outcomes.
3. Test externally supplied level facts flow through Not and external-output observation without transformation at the boundary.
4. Instrument or otherwise prove every represented reaction operation executes exactly once and only after each predecessor result is available.
5. Run focused tests while iterating, then make check-dev; final acceptance additionally runs make check-final.

## Dependencies

- Roadmap item 13 / ms-d1f is complete and accepted.
- Roadmap item 15 adds the validated public InputSnapshot artifact; this bead intentionally consumes only raw supplied level facts.

## Readiness

Ready for implementation. The remaining choices are ordinary deterministic implementation freedom; no conflicting requirement, missing fundamental semantic rule, or frozen compatibility promise blocks this restricted reference-evaluator slice.

title: Implement initialization transaction execution
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 18: execute the first restricted level initialization transaction against an `AwaitingInitialization` machine at an arbitrary logical time. Use one complete exact-bound `InputSnapshot`, the ordinary full Constant/Not evaluator, and correctness-oriented atomic staging. Success publishes one complete `Ready` machine and deterministic external `LevelEstablished` events; rejection leaves the complete machine unchanged.

## Contract basis

- `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction` (`docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml`), reviewed at the current evidence baseline, governs the explicit transaction value, exact preconditions, policy budgets, ordinary evaluation, Ready commit, output establishment, provenance, atomicity, and verification.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle` (`docs/specs/contracts/machine-lifecycle.yaml`), reviewed and implemented by `ms-puk`, supplies the canonical machine ownership and `AwaitingInitialization` state consumed here.
- `mossignal.runtime.level_input_snapshot`, `mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator`, `mossignal.compile.compiled_network`, and `mossignal.runtime.policy` are reviewed and used unchanged for exact snapshot binding, settlement, immutable topology, and applicable budget behavior.

## Included scope

- Add the owned level-only `Transaction<D>::initialize(Time<D>, NetworkRevision, InputSnapshot<D>)` form and restricted `Machine::apply` path.
- Require `AwaitingInitialization`, an exact current revision, and snapshot identities matching the machine's exact `NetworkKey`, `NetworkFingerprint`, and `InputSchemaFingerprint`.
- Feed the snapshot's complete stable-keyed authoritative external levels to the existing ordinary full Constant/Not evaluator; do not create a special initialization evaluator or infer omitted inputs as `Low`.
- Validate the associated runtime policy and enforce each semantic budget that has a real accounting boundary in this execution path.
- Stage all fallible work against one complete private candidate and publish once through a non-fallible commit point.
- On success, establish the requested time, preserve revision and policy identity, store authoritative external levels, complete settled levels, and every external level-output baseline, and transition to `Ready`.
- Return one `LevelEstablished` event for each external level output, including a zero-length stream for an empty output set. Order same-time events canonically by stable output identity, independently of topology construction, map iteration, and dense storage order.
- Give every returned establishment event an opaque `CauseRef`; the owned immutable result must retain a `ProvenanceView` resolving every returned cause to a structured acyclic derivation with authoritative initialization roots.
- Preserve structured catalogue distinctions for every reachable lifecycle, revision, input-compatibility, evaluation, and budget rejection.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No `InputDelta`, ready-machine execution, successful repeat initialization, pulse I/O, stateful or temporal nodes, pending events, deadlines, schedules, runtime occurrences, or persistent diagnostic episodes.
- No topology patch, migration, revision advancement, reconfiguration, persistence, replay, restoration, forecast, observer delivery, public callbacks, or optimized sparse/copy-on-write staging.
- No execution or observable state digests, machine snapshot, or complete explanation-oriented provenance beyond what returned initialization events require.
- Do not change reviewed snapshot, evaluator, compiled-network, lifecycle, or runtime-policy contracts unless implementation discovers a reusable specification-backed correction; any such change returns to draft review.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Private transaction, candidate-state, settled-result, event, provenance, and failure storage; module placement; accessor details; and canonical sorting mechanism are free when the reviewed contracts remain exact.
- Use the simplest auditable clone-and-swap mechanism. Private staging does not create a public `Machine<D>: Clone` promise.
- Keep result and failure fields private or non-exhaustive as appropriate so this bounded slice does not freeze unrelated later compatibility promises. Reachable failures must remain structured and every returned cause must resolve.
- Do not invent counters for unsupported subsystems. Record and test ordinary deterministic representation choices in the implementation or close-out.

## Required verification

1. Initialize equivalent machines at zero and an arbitrary nonzero time; verify `Ready { now }`, unchanged revision and policy identity, authoritative external levels, complete settled levels, and output baselines.
2. Cover representative Constant, external-input/output, Not, chained, fan-out, multiple-input, multiple-output, and empty-output restricted networks through the ordinary full evaluator.
3. Verify every external level output produces one exact deterministic `LevelEstablished` whose cause resolves through the result, and that insertion/construction order cannot perturb the stream.
4. Verify lifecycle incompatibility, stale revision, wrong network, wrong fingerprint/schema, and every other reachable rejection preserve complete semantic machine equality.
5. For every implemented runtime-policy accounting boundary, test one below, exactly at, and one above the limit where representable, including complete rollback on failure.
6. Run focused tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`; final acceptance additionally runs `make check-final`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A complete exact-bound level snapshot initializes an `AwaitingInitialization` restricted machine at any representable logical time through the ordinary full evaluator.
- Success publishes one complete Ready state with authoritative and settled storage plus deterministic establishment events whose causes resolve through the owned result, without changing topology revision or policy association.
- Every supported rejection is structured and proves complete semantic machine equality before and after application.
- The implementation remains inside the reviewed Constant/Not, level-only, correctness-oriented staging boundary and passes the required gates.

## Dependencies and readiness

`ms-puk` is closed and accepted, and roadmap items 13 through 16 already supply compilation, full evaluation, complete level snapshots, and runtime policy. This bead is open, unblocked, reviewed, and implementation-ready. No conflicting requirement, missing fundamental semantic rule, or frozen compatibility promise blocks the bounded slice.
notes:
Implementation close-out:
- Added owned explicit initialization transactions and atomic Machine application for the restricted Constant/Not runtime.
- Promoted the existing full topological evaluator from test-only to crate-private production staging and retained complete settled operation values.
- Added authoritative external-level storage, output baselines, Ready lifecycle transition, deterministic LevelEstablished events, and result-owned provenance resolution.
- Chose stable ExternalOutputKey order as the canonical same-time event representation.
- Chose result-scoped opaque CauseRef values with a deterministic private scope plus ordinal; no durable representation or private arena position is exposed.
- Implemented semantic accounting for one internal reaction, compiled operation evaluations, emitted output events, and required provenance records. Pending-event accounting remains absent because initialization creates no pending work in this restricted slice.
- Added exact structured lifecycle, stale-revision, wrong-network, foreign-schema, and budget rejection categories with atomic rollback.

Verification:
- Focused initialization tests: passed (6 tests)
- Workspace tests: passed (103 tests)
- make check-dev: passed
- make check-final: passed

Corrective acceptance review:
- Audited the committed implementation against the reviewed initialization-transaction and machine-lifecycle contracts.
- Strengthened complete-machine rollback observations for every reachable structured rejection and applicable budget failure.
- Added equivalent zero-time and nonzero-time initialization coverage, including revision and runtime-policy identity retention.
- Strengthened causal verification so every returned establishment cause is acyclic and terminates in authoritative initialization roots.
- Completed documentation for the bounded TransactionResult accessors.

Review verification:
- Focused initialization tests: passed (7 tests)
- make check-dev: passed
- make check-final: passed

title: Commit one prepared topology patch through the ordinary transaction
description:
## Objective and baseline

Implement roadmap item 58, `Atomic topology replacement and migration`, from `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`.

Preparation baseline: `07f960e70b12e5c2e38c8a9b27fb77896360b65c` (`ms-ucj: prepare one topology replacement without mutating the machine`), on main. Governing specifications were unchanged when this bead was derived. The roadmap is sequencing context, not product authority. Item 57 stays done. Do not reopen `ms-ucj`. Do not start item 59 or later.

Commit one already prepared topology patch through the ordinary transaction boundary. Finalization reads the machine state reached at the effective time, applies the prepared static plan, and publishes one atomic result. A v1 label, golden, persistence design, public type, or stability wording is not a freeze. Do not add a patch-format, snapshot-format, replay-format, or catalogue freeze.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contract governing this item

- `mossignal.reconfiguration.atomic_replacement`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/atomic-topology-replacement.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs attachment, effective-time finalization, loss policy, the migration report, atomic publication, and snapshot sufficiency of the committed machine

### Reviewed contracts used unchanged

- `mossignal.reconfiguration.structural_preparation`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/structural-preparation.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: the prepared patch and static plan are inputs; do not re-derive or reopen them
- `mossignal.runtime.transaction_forecast`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/transaction-forecast.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: once a transaction carries a patch, forecast uses the same transition and does not publish
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-lifecycle.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: only a committed patch advances `NetworkRevision`
- `mossignal.persistence.machine_snapshot_restoration`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-snapshot-restoration.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: restoration of the committed machine must not apply a patch
- `mossignal.persistence.replay_artifacts`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/replay-artifacts.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: the current codec stays patch-free and keeps its fail-closed patch-child rejection

`known_uncovered` names persisted patch and migration-report artifacts, patch-bearing replay frames, transaction metadata, collaborative editing, incremental compilation, caller migration functions, and catalogue modules this runtime does not construct. Those facets are outside this bead.

## Included scope

- `Transaction::with_patch` and `Transaction::expect_execution_state` for one initialization or advancement transaction.
- Explicit `ReconfigurationPolicy::{RejectStateLoss, AllowReportedStateLoss}` supplied by the caller.
- Ready-machine ordering: earlier deadlines under the old topology, finalization against the state immediately before the effective time, target installation in candidate state, one target reaction, atomic publication.
- Initialization ordering from base declared initial state, with a complete target-bound snapshot and no prior pending work.
- Application of the prepared plan to state, pending events, valuations, baselines, episodes, and provenance, including module internals.
- One complete migration report, revision advance to the prepared proposed revision, and ordinary result publication.
- Catalogue finalization failures and full-transaction rollback.
- Snapshot round-trip of the committed machine and later patch-free replay from that machine.
- Forecast of the same patch-bearing transaction through the existing shared transition.

## Exclusions

- Structural preparation, correspondence, and static-plan classification.
- Persisted `network_patch`, `migration_report`, and patch-bearing replay frames. Do not re-prepare a decoded patch during replay.
- `Transaction::with_meta`.
- Collaborative editing, rebase, merge, inverse patches, and an incremental patch compiler.
- A hidden default loss policy or a caller-supplied migration callback.
- Name-based migration and one-to-many identity.
- Items 59 and later.

## Implementation obligations

Follow the reviewed rules `patch-bearing-transaction`, `effective-time-order`, `initialization-patch`, `finalize-prepared-plan`, `input-output-and-cause`, `explicit-loss-policy`, `migration-report`, `revision-provenance-and-episodes`, `atomic-failure`, `committed-snapshot-and-later-replay`, `forecast-shares-the-transition`, and `finalization-verification`.

`Transaction::with_patch` returns `Result<Self, TransactionBuildFailure<D>>`. It rejects every base-revision, network, target-schema, lifecycle, and time-domain mismatch determinable from the transaction and the prepared patch. The prepared base revision must equal the transaction's expected revision, and the input must be bound to the prepared target schema. An initialization transaction carries a target-bound `InputSnapshot`. An advancement transaction carries a target-bound `InputDelta`. Those input kinds are fixed by the transaction constructors. Applying initialization to a ready machine fails with `lifecycle.already_initialized`. Applying advancement to an uninitialized machine fails with `lifecycle.delta_before_initialization`.

Before candidate work, the prepared patch matches the machine only when the machine network key, machine revision, machine fingerprint, prepared base revision, prepared base fingerprint, signal-semantics version, and runtime time domain are equal. Inequality is `reconfiguration.stale_prepared_patch`. A transaction expected revision that differs from the machine is `runtime.stale_revision`. A ready requested time that is not strictly later than the current logical time is `runtime.time_not_strictly_increasing`. A supplied execution digest that does not match rejects with `runtime.stale_execution_state` before candidate work.

Events strictly before the effective time run under the old topology and are discarded if the outer transaction fails. Events due at the effective time are migrated before they fire. Same-time input is not migration state. The patch is a cause and is not a synthetic signal. The observable target reaction matches complete evaluation of the target graph.

`RejectStateLoss` rejects a nonempty finalized loss set. An unrealized conditional loss does not reject. `AllowReportedStateLoss` commits only when every possible loss category was classified during preparation and every actual loss appears in the committed report. Install `PreparedPatch::proposed_revision` on success only.

Add the catalogue section 35 finalization codes that are not yet delivered, with their recorded severity, responsibility, evidence, and failure delivery. The closed reconfiguration failure family also delivers `reconfiguration.ambiguous_event_migration` and `reconfiguration.conflicting_migrated_transitions` when finalization discovers those conditions. The first code is already registered; register the second. Do not emit finalization codes from preparation. Checked time and budget failures stay `runtime.time_overflow` and `runtime.budget_exceeded`.

A recording helper must reject a patch-bearing transaction without writing a patch-free frame and without mutating the machine. Leave the existing `replay.patch_preparation_diverged` rejection of a patch child in place.

Where the specifications allow several conforming choices, choose the simplest deterministic option, test it, and record it. Do not amend specifications first. If implementation finds a concrete contradiction in the reviewed contract, return only that contract to draft and do not refresh reviewed hashes of contracts that were not re-audited.

## Implementation freedom

- Complete target-graph evaluation is sufficient. An incremental compiler is not required.
- Private candidate storage and opaque report accessors are sufficient.
- Do not invent a second successor-revision encoding.
- Rejecting patch-bearing recording is sufficient until a patch-bearing frame exists.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs` and the machine apply path.
- `crates/mossignal/src/diagnostics.rs` and the diagnostic and failure goldens, only for finalization codes that are not already present.
- Public re-exports in `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs` for the new commitment types.
- Integration tests for commitment, atomicity, snapshot restoration, later patch-free replay, and forecast equivalence.
- A narrow guard in the replay recording path so a patch-bearing transaction is not stored as a patch-free frame.

Do not edit `docs/specs/contracts/structural-preparation.yaml`, `transaction-forecast.yaml`, `replay-artifacts.yaml`, or `machine-snapshot-restoration.yaml` unless a concrete contradiction appears.

## Verification

- Earlier deadlines change state, and the later patch migrates that reached state.
- Both loss policies, including an unrealized conditional loss.
- Temporal obligations strictly before, at, and after the effective time.
- Preserved, established, and removed level outputs, and a pulse caused by changed connectivity.
- One module-internal loss rejects the whole transaction under `RejectStateLoss`.
- A failure after earlier deadline work leaves the published machine unchanged.
- A determinable schema or base-revision mismatch is rejected before application, and a stale fingerprint or revision at application is `reconfiguration.stale_prepared_patch`.
- Forecast of the patch transaction matches cloned apply and does not publish.
- A snapshot of the committed machine restores an equivalent machine against the target network, and a later patch-free replay matches continued execution. Replay boundaries immediately before and after the commit use those snapshot checkpoints and patch-free logs.
- Use narrow tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`. Acceptance separately runs `make check-final`.
- Do not weaken a test, oracle, lint, or gate.

## Blocking questions

None. The persisted patch-frame format is `known_uncovered`, not a missing rule for this commit. No explicit maintainer freeze names this surface.

## Readiness

Open and ready for implementation. The governing contract `mossignal.reconfiguration.atomic_replacement` is reviewed. Do not implement a persisted patch frame, and do not reopen the adjacent reviewed contracts unless a concrete contradiction appears.
notes:
Completed roadmap item 58 on main by continuing the inherited in-progress proposal. Transactions can attach one prepared patch with an explicit loss policy and optional execution-state precondition. Earlier deadlines run under the source topology; finalization reads the reached state, installs the target only in candidate storage, performs complete target evaluation, and publishes topology, revision, migration report, outputs, diagnostics, and provenance atomically. Forecast uses the same transition. Patch-bearing recording is rejected before mutation; committed target snapshots support ordinary restoration and later patch-free replay.

Corrective acceptance added regression coverage for reset and removed-owner provenance, dense-slot reassignment, per-event cancellation and loss identities, pre-patch reset_to predicates, episode termination and reassociated episode owners, source-identity report ordering, new input establishment, separate source/target operation costs, exactly-due recomputed obligations, periodic anchor ordinals and target cadence, immediate reanchoring, and named timing rules in scheduling ancestry. title: Add SampleHold primitive
description:
## Objective and baseline

Implement roadmap item 45, `SampleHold`, from `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md` after accepted 44B (`ms-6af`, closed). Add the distinct Level-value/Pulse-sample primitive through the ordinary authoring, validation, compilation, stateful evaluation, inspection, and provenance paths.

Preparation baseline: `e7a72dab3cbf1bab3630374465755e2ee67a9dc3` on `main`, initially clean. Governing specifications and existing contracts have no working-tree changes. There were no open or active beads. The roadmap supplies sequencing context; specifications and the contracts below supply the semantic basis.

## Contract basis

### Independently reviewed SampleHold contract

- `mossignal.node.sample_hold` — `docs/specs/contracts/sample-hold.yaml` — **reviewed**. Required facets: `fixed-shape-and-initial-level`, `settled-sampling-law`, `shape-validation-and-current-dependencies`, `typed-and-dynamic-authoring`, `semantic-identity-facets`, `held-state-inspection-and-causality`, and `sample-hold-conformance`. This bead selects the `exhaustive-sampling-domain` recommendation as mandatory finite verification. Snapshot/replay/digest and topology-migration coverage remain known later integration.

### Reviewed contracts reused unchanged

- `mossignal.runtime.stateful_reaction_foundation` — `docs/specs/contracts/stateful-reaction-foundation.yaml`: previous/proposed state, declared-state initialization, current-output causality, family storage, atomic commitment, owned inspection, and stateful verification.
- `mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation` — `docs/specs/contracts/reaction-scoped-pulse-foundation.yaml`: complete reaction-local counts, typed exact-bound input batches, fan-out, initialization/ready integration, grouped provenance, overflow atomicity, and pulse conformance. Do not rely on its older `pre-stability-pulse-identity-extension` rule whose projection citation changed; identity is covered separately below.
- `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction` — `docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml` and `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction` — `docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml`: lifecycle/input boundaries, ordinary settlement, output establishment/change distinction, owned causal results, applicable budgets, and complete failure preservation. Their opening Constant/Not scope is extended by the node/stateful/pulse contracts, not used to limit the evaluator to those nodes.
- `mossignal.module.aware_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/module-aware-execution.yaml`: ordinary recursive primitive lowering, independent qualified state owners, transparent settlement and budgets, retained hierarchy, qualified inspection/provenance, and module execution verification.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint` — `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`: deterministic semantic identity, representation exclusions, and golden-vector verification; the new SampleHold contract owns its additional kind/configuration/role/state facets. `mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint` — `docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml`: complete user-module projection, representation exclusions, and deterministic/configuration-sensitive identity.
- `mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder` — `docs/specs/contracts/typed-network-builder.yaml` and `mossignal.authoring.typed_module_builder` — `docs/specs/contracts/typed-module-builder.yaml`: scoped typed signals, foreign-signal failures, explicit identity rejection, module primitive-family parity, canonical lowering, and ordinary completion.
- `mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition` — `docs/specs/contracts/authored-network-definition.yaml`: stable typed dynamic records, preservation of malformed claims (including duplicate keys and wrong-kind/direction incidence), and the structured validation transition. Reuse these unchanged general facets; SampleHold's fixed shape and law remain owned by its node contract.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model` — `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`: existing structured authoring/validation/inspection failures, exact safe code/evidence/delivery associations, useful stable subjects, registry conformance, and failure inventories.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy` — `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`: existing semantic budgets, atomic budget failure, and implemented-boundary checks. No new policy family.
- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`: chronological internal reactions, exact-target batching, direct-jump equivalence, owned chronological results, and single outer-transaction publication when existing PulseDelay nodes deliver sample pulses.

Every reused facet above is backed by unchanged reviewed sources. No existing contract is reopened. The current-reaction-dependency contract was inspected as a candidate, but this bead does not depend on its changed compilation-verification citation; SampleHold's signature and the stateful foundation directly govern the needed dependency behavior.

## Included scope

1. Add `SampleHoldConfig` with explicit `initial: LogicLevel` and the closed SampleHold node. Its fixed ports are `value: Level`, `sample: Pulse`, and one Level output. Provide typed `sample_hold`, explicit `add_sample_hold`, exact-port construction, and dynamic authoring on both network and module paths. Follow existing Result/AddedNode conventions and preserve exact roles, kinds, identities, and configuration through lowering.
2. Extend the central node schema and ordinary validation/compilation machinery. Both inputs are conservative current-output dependencies even when the current sample count is zero. Reject malformed roles/kinds/arity, missing or extra connections, duplicate identities, and instantaneous feedback through either influence path using existing structured failure categories.
3. Apply the law once per logical reaction: zero samples retain previous stored level; any positive complete count captures the fully settled current value. Return that value downstream immediately and stage one successor. Initialization uses declared initial state as previous state, processes its initial sample batch, and publishes only the complete successful machine. Positive counts greater than one must not create repeated same-time transitions.
4. Reuse the accepted shared stored-level value/proposed-state family for Toggle and both latches. This is a task-specific choice building on the accepted implementation, not a permanent representation promise. Preserve independent direct and fully qualified module owners without adding a parallel Boolean value vector or general arbitrary-state framework.
5. Provide focused owned SampleHold definition/current inspection: stable owner, configuration, declared versus committed held value, applicable current Level input/output, time/revision, and causal facts. Runtime inspection before initialization uses the existing not-initialized category. Pulse activity must not become a persistent current signal; any retained count is explicitly reaction/capture evidence. Integrate held state and its cause into module inspection without aliasing instances.
6. Retain capture causality sufficient to explain the sampled Level and every grouped sample contributor, including counts and qualified owners. On retention, preserve the authoritative history establishing the held value. Distinguish current support, held-state establishment, and latest output transition; unchanged Level output emits no fabricated transition. Retained inspection/results and their CauseRefs remain meaningful through later transactions.
7. Include the SampleHold kind, typed roles, explicit initial level, and stored-level schema in deterministic network and module identity. Extend the current provisional projection in place with the simplest coherent encoding and representative golden bytes/digest; no historical readers or compatibility shims. Update public failure inventories for any added inspection leaves and closed-kind classification machinery.
8. Keep all SampleHold successor, inspection evidence, outputs, provenance, and any internal-deadline effects in the existing candidate transaction. Rejections or budget failures after staged captures preserve the complete published machine and earlier retained results. SampleHold itself adds no pending-event owner, temporal scheduling law, conflict policy, or successful diagnostic condition.

## Implementation freedom

- Choose the simplest deterministic private descriptors, helper names, exact-port API grouping, and state-cause map organization consistent with existing architecture. Extending a shared cause map or adding a focused SampleHold cause map is allowed; preserve node-specific meanings and avoid broad cleanup.
- Choose, test, and record the cause refresh rule for capturing an already-held value. A simple option is that every positive sample establishes a capture cause, including same-value captures, while zero samples retain the old establishment. Whichever rule is chosen, all current sample contributors remain explainable and the latest output-transition cause remains unchanged when output does not change.
- Focused accessors and an owned capture-evidence shape are sufficient; do not implement a general StateChange collection, explanation-query engine, or recent-history API to fill eventual public shapes.
- Choose deterministic canonical SampleHold kind/role tags and state-schema encoding, test identity sensitivity and construction-order invariance, and record the choice. No release freeze or specification amendment is needed before exercising this bounded freedom.
- No unresolved product question. Implementation-discovered reusable specification facts may be preserved in draft contracts, but require independent review before final acceptance. Ordinary representation choices are recorded in tests/close-out rather than promoted to product policy.

## Required verification

1. Exhaust all eight combinations of previous held level, current value level, and sample absence/presence independently for initialization and Ready reactions. For Ready cases first establish the intended prior state independently; do not merely repeat a post-initialization result. Refine presence with counts 0, 1, 2, and a large representable count, including `u64::MAX` where directly supplied. Verify same-value sampling, value changes without sampling, successive captures, and no cross-reaction pulse persistence.
2. Compare typed, explicit-keyed, and equivalent dynamic network/module authoring. Cover exact-port and connection-order permutations, foreign signals on either input, duplicate stable identities, malformed fixed shape/kinds/roles, and conservative dependency/cycle behavior through both the Level value path and Pulse sample path. Use existing cycle diagnostics and witnesses.
3. Prove same-reaction capture of an upstream stateful node's newly settled value and SampleHold -> FallingEdge propagation, including a chain where the same pulse feeds an upstream Toggle and the sample port. Add a composed capture/retain history compared with a small direct reference recurrence; changing insertion/input order cannot change behavior.
4. Verify one shared stored-level family with correct slot/owner correspondence and independent state across mixed Toggle/latch/SampleHold nodes, multiple instances of one module, and a nested module. Retain qualified inspection and causal ownership; compare explicit and module-wrapped behavior after normalizing only intentionally distinct structural identity.
5. Check configuration-sensitive network and module fingerprints, distinct node/port roles, identity invariance under insertion/metadata/private-layout differences, and representative canonical projection bytes/digest. Keep identity-sensitive and merely behaviorally equivalent comparisons distinct.
6. Check preinitialization structural inspection and runtime rejection; declared versus captured state; exact capture evidence and grouped contributors for multiple sample sources; causal paths to the sampled value and authoritative roots. Verify the chosen same-value capture convention, zero-sample retention, current-support changes without a new output transition, and old owned results/inspection causes after later captures.
7. Use existing PulseDelay composition to sample at internal deadlines and at a requested time shared with external Level changes. Compare a direct time jump with stepwise advancement for final held state, chronological output events, schedule, and causal meaning. Distinct deadlines must sample the value at each actual reaction rather than coalesce into one capture.
8. Force rejection after candidate captures, including a later failure after an earlier internal deadline. Compare complete published state: lifecycle/time/revision, external valuation, settled values, stored levels and causes, active episodes, pending events/cursor, outputs/baselines, schedule, and provenance. Cover existing output-event/provenance budget boundaries below/at/above where representable; earlier retained results remain valid. Test a narrow SampleHold-caused capture followed by an existing rejection path instead of inventing a new runtime failure category.
9. Explicitly classify the conformance inventory: no SampleHold-owned due events, scheduling, conflict diagnostics, or episode lifecycle; persistence/replay/topology/migration are later integration rather than implemented claims. Verify catalogue/failure inventory coherence for added public inspection leaves.
10. Run focused SampleHold, stateful, pulse, edge, module, temporal, provenance, transaction, identity, and diagnostic tests; then `make check-dev`. Corrective final acceptance also requires `make check-final` and synchronized closed-bead acceptance checks under repository policy.

## Exclusions

No resettable standard modules or optional reset port; payload/analog/integer values; counters or generic memory/state machines; new temporal primitives or event-calendar changes; state history or general explanation queries; observer/subscription APIs; new conflict diagnostics or episode producers; snapshot/restore/replay/digest APIs; topology patches, migration, or reset implementation; evaluator optimizations; compatibility shims or release-readiness baseline.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/{authored,builder,node_schema,lib}.rs`: configuration, fixed roles/kinds, network/module constructors, exports.
- `crates/mossignal/src/{validation,compile,identity}.rs`: validation classifications, closed descriptors, shared state layout/evaluation, canonical identity.
- `crates/mossignal/src/{machine,transaction}.rs`: focused inspection, capture/state provenance, candidate state integration and complete rollback observations.
- `crates/mossignal/src/diagnostics.rs` only for required closed-kind/leaf integration, plus focused tests such as `crates/mossignal/tests/sample_hold.rs` and affected goldens.
- Close this bead, synchronize `.beads`, and mark roadmap item 45 DONE only after implementation. Preserve the closed predecessor and accepted 44B work.

## Research disposition and readiness

SampleHold's symbols and sample-and-hold aliases were searched across authoritative specs. Its law, shape, API/configuration, dependency signature, state inspection and causal requirements, fingerprint facets, and finite/stateful-chain verification map to the independently reviewed SampleHold contract. Generic lifecycle, pulse-count, atomicity, module, identity, authoring, diagnostic, budget, and chronology rules reuse the unchanged reviewed facets above. The earlier API's descriptive `Sample` spelling denotes the same Level-sampled-by-Pulse concept; the built-in and concrete API documents name it SampleHold. Standard-catalogue resettable expansions and reconfiguration's Boolean-state family were identified as adjacent future consumers, not added to this primitive slice.

Open, approved, and ready for bounded implementation with no product blocker or deferred design dependency. Independent review checked every cited SampleHold section, bounded discovery and applicable contract seams, promoted the SampleHold contract with all 17 current source hashes, and confirmed the stated implementation freedoms and exclusions. The authored-network contract was added to make ownership of malformed dynamic claims and their validation boundary explicit; no implementation scope or decomposition changed.
acceptance_criteria: Implement roadmap 45 SampleHold with fixed Level value/Pulse sample authoring, schema and validation; settled presence-based capture through the shared stored-level family; immediate downstream output and atomic successor commitment; owned qualified inspection and capture provenance; deterministic network/module identity; exhaustive independent initialization/Ready laws, causal ownership, deadline equivalence, and complete rollback checks. Preserve documented exclusions and implementation freedom. make check-dev passes; final acceptance requires make check-final and synchronized closed-bead records. SampleHold contract and this bounded bead are independently reviewed and approved for implementation; all required contract sources are current for the reused facets.

title: Add Coalesce and Zip pulse primitives
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Continuation Roadmap item 41 as one bounded pulse-combinational expansion: add Coalesce and Zip across both typed builders and the canonical dynamic, validation, compilation, execution, provenance, identity, and transaction paths while preserving their distinct reaction-local multiplicity laws.

## Roadmap provenance

- Document: `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`
- Item: 41
- Title: Remaining pulse-combinational primitives

This provenance records sequencing only. The referenced contracts and authoritative specifications govern product semantics.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed feature contract

- `mossignal.node.pulse_combinational_expansion`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/pulse-combinational-expansion.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs Coalesce and Zip laws, port and arity domains, authoring, validation, causality, settlement, provenance, fingerprint integration, and conformance.

### Reviewed contracts reused without modification

- `mossignal.node.pulse_merge` (`docs/specs/contracts/pulse-merge.yaml`): unchanged variadic Pulse port identity, typed and dynamic authoring pattern, dependency/compilation integration, grouped provenance, advisories, and conformance pattern.
- `mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation` (`docs/specs/contracts/reaction-scoped-pulse-foundation.yaml`): typed reaction-scoped counts, fan-out, input and transaction integration, output publication, grouped provenance, and failure atomicity. Its changed restricted-fingerprint source facet was rechecked directly for this task and is refined by the reviewed feature contract.
- `mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition` (`docs/specs/contracts/authored-network-definition.yaml`) and `mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder` (`docs/specs/contracts/typed-network-builder.yaml`): canonical unchecked node/port/connection representation and builder-scoped typed Signal rules.
- `mossignal.authoring.typed_module_builder` (`docs/specs/contracts/typed-module-builder.yaml`): unchanged primitive-family parity, explicit module-local identity, canonical unchecked lowering, and foreign-signal rejection for ModuleBuilder.
- `mossignal.graph.structural_validation` (`docs/specs/contracts/structural-validation.yaml`), `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_dependency_graph` (`docs/specs/contracts/current-reaction-dependency-graph.yaml`), and `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_cycle_validation` (`docs/specs/contracts/current-reaction-cycle-validation.yaml`): existing stable-subject validation, dependency, and acyclicity boundaries. Only the task-relevant generic facets apply; changed validated-owner and verification source facets do not alter the node laws researched here.
- `mossignal.compile.compiled_network` (`docs/specs/contracts/compiled-network.yaml`) and `mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator` (`docs/specs/contracts/restricted-full-topological-evaluator.yaml`): immutable descriptors, stable-to-dense privacy, compiled invariants, and complete deterministic settlement.
- `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction` (`docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml`) and `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction` (`docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml`): canonical lifecycle, result, provenance, budget, and failure-atomic transaction behavior reused for pulse-bearing reactions.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint` (`docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`) and `mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint` (`docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml`): semantic node-kind, port, incidence, ordering, and metadata-exclusion identity rules. The accepted implementation must synchronize the provisional exact network projection and affected evidence after the concrete variants are chosen.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model` (`docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`) and `mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports` (`docs/specs/contracts/artifact-reports.yaml`): catalogue-backed structured validation findings and non-blocking artifact-bearing reports.

## Included scope

- Add closed dynamic `NodeKind::Coalesce` and `NodeKind::Zip` support with one Pulse output, exactly one Pulse input for Coalesce, and one or more stable variadic Pulse inputs for Zip.
- Add concise and explicit keyed Coalesce and Zip construction to both `NetworkBuilder<D>` and `ModuleBuilder<D>`, preserving immediate iterator consumption, builder ownership checks, exact-key dynamic reconstruction, and canonical lowering.
- Extend structural validation for fixed shape, Pulse kinds, missing ports, Zip zero arity, unary Zip advisories, and duplicate-source advisories where applicable.
- Extend current-reaction dependency extraction, cycle validation, compilation, compiled invariants, and full topological evaluation using every Pulse input-to-output influence.
- Implement Coalesce as zero-to-zero and positive-to-one, retaining complete causal support despite the bounded output count.
- Implement Zip as the reaction-local minimum input count, with one unordered all-port group per output occurrence and no retention of unmatched counts.
- Integrate exact initialization and ready-transaction Pulse output behavior, grouped provenance, runtime budgets, and complete failure atomicity through the existing machine path.
- Extend provisional network and module semantic fingerprint coverage for the two distinct node kinds and stable port incidences, synchronizing authoritative projection text, implementation, affected contract evidence, and golden vectors without historical compatibility machinery.
- Add reusable conformance and focused integration tests for both typed builders, direct dynamic definitions, diagnostics, determinism, provenance, transactions, and identity.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No PulseGate, PulseSelect, PulseRoute, edge detector, additional stateful node, or temporal node.
- No level-controlled behavior, payload transport, pulse persistence, pending event, deadline, schedule change, or unmatched-count buffering.
- No new external input/output artifact semantics, transaction API, evaluator architecture, runtime policy category, provenance identity model, or diagnostic namespace beyond applying existing conditions.
- No standard-module `any_pulse` convenience; it remains later catalogue/convenience work even though Coalesce makes its expansion possible.
- No general node inspection, current explanation, why-not rendering, snapshot codec, replay codec, topology patch, migration, or compatibility shim.
- No compatibility migration for earlier provisional fingerprints or goldens; the repository is pre-release and the accepted revision must only be internally coherent.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement reviewed contract requirements `coalesce-unary-law`, `coalesce-retains-causal-support`, `zip-group-law`, `zip-port-identity-and-reaction-isolation`, `typed-and-dynamic-authoring`, `structural-validation-and-findings`, `causality-compilation-and-settlement`, `bounded-checked-count-results`, `joint-group-provenance`, `pre-stability-fingerprint-extension`, and `primitive-conformance`.
- Reuse the existing Merge and Pulse foundation representations and evaluator path rather than adding a parallel pulse store, transaction path, or callback boundary.
- Preserve stable port incidence and signal kind through unchecked definitions, validation candidates, dependency vertices, compiled descriptors, provenance subjects, and fingerprints; dense positions remain private revision-local implementation details.
- Make zero-input Zip a blocking `validation.invalid_variadic_arity` finding, unary Zip a valid artifact with `validation.unary_degenerate_node`, and malformed Coalesce shapes use the existing fixed-shape and kind-aware validation conditions.
- Preserve complete reaction batches: Coalesce must not lose upstream causal support when bounding the count, Zip must use every settled input count jointly, and neither node may carry unmatched Pulse occurrences into a later reaction.
- Ensure typed and direct dynamic construction of equal stable structures produces equivalent validation, dependency graphs, compiled behavior, provenance, and fingerprints in both network and reusable-module contexts.
- Keep production code free of `unwrap` and `expect`.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose the smallest deterministic private descriptor variants, evaluator helpers, minimum-reduction strategy, and grouped-provenance record shape compatible with existing provenance inspection; test and record the concrete choice.
- Choose deterministic locally allocated fixed-port and variadic-port ordering consistent with existing builder patterns. Exact keyed forms remain the durable reconstruction authority.
- Choose exact provisional canonical variant spellings for Coalesce and Zip, update authority and goldens coherently, and do not add readers, migrations, aliases, or deprecations for the prior repository revision.
- Reuse or extract shared NetworkBuilder and ModuleBuilder helpers where that reduces duplication without merging their distinct builder scopes.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/authored.rs` and `crates/mossignal/src/builder.rs` for dynamic kinds and NetworkBuilder construction.
- `crates/mossignal/src/module.rs` or existing module-builder support for primitive-family parity and canonical lowering.
- `crates/mossignal/src/validation.rs` for Coalesce shape and Zip arity/quality findings.
- `crates/mossignal/src/compile.rs` for descriptors, dependency-preserving compilation, invariant checks, evaluation, and grouped provenance inputs.
- `crates/mossignal/src/identity.rs` and the authoritative restricted fingerprint projection for exact kind variants and golden vectors.
- `crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs` only as narrowly required for canonical grouped causes or conformance access; no separate application path.

title: Add level-controlled pulse primitives
description:
## Objective

Changed generic source facets were rechecked directly and do not alter this family.

## Included scope

- Add concise and exact keyed constructors to NetworkBuilder and ModuleBuilder. PulseRoute exposes distinct typed when-low and when-high outputs.
- Extend structural validation for fixed arity, signal kinds, required drivers, semantic roles, duplicate claims, and independently safe findings using existing conditions.
- Extend dependency extraction, cycle validation, compilation, invariants, and full topological execution for every conservative input-to-output influence.
- Implement PulseGate as High-pass and Low-suppress, PulseSelect as complete selected-branch multiplicity, and PulseRoute as complete count on exactly one selected output.
- Settle simultaneous controls and counts without consumption, buffering, hidden ordering, stored enable state, or pulse persistence.
- Retain resolvable event provenance for the controlling Level fact and passed or selected Pulse batch.
- Extend provisional network and module fingerprints for all three kinds and every semantic role, including PulseRoute output roles, synchronizing authority, implementation, and exact golden vectors.
- Add focused reusable conformance for typed, direct dynamic, module-wrapped, malformed, multi-layer, and transaction cases.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No edge detectors, state cells, stored enable state, pulse persistence, temporal windows, deadlines, pending events, callbacks, or host effects.

3. Exercise simultaneous control changes and pulse observations during initialization and multiple ready reactions; verify no stored enable or cross-reaction persistence.
4. Compare NetworkBuilder, ModuleBuilder, exact keyed, and direct dynamic forms for shapes, roles, validation, dependencies, compilation, execution, provenance, and identity.
5. Exercise malformed arity, wrong kinds, missing drivers, duplicate keys, role defects, multiple drivers, and cycles through structured deterministic diagnostics.
6. Verify all dependency edges, multi-layer fan-out and reconvergence, and order invariance without traversal intermediates or pulse consumption.
7. Verify nonzero event provenance resolves to current control and passed or selected support; suppressed paths do not become emitted contributors or retained state.
8. Verify identity sensitivity to node kind, every input and route-output role, port key, incidence, NetworkKey, TimeDomainId, and module structure; verify insertion-order and metadata invariance with complete canonical bytes and digests.
9. Force applicable upstream overflow and runtime-budget failures around all three nodes and compare complete machine observations before and after rejection.
10. Run focused tests while iterating, then make check-dev; final acceptance additionally runs make check-final.

## Blocking questions

Bounded and claimable with no product-semantics blocker. The governing feature contract is reviewed and reusable at its recorded evidence baseline.
